# Ashes of Empires, Cycle Log

The loop's memory. Read before every cycle, append after every cycle.

## Cycle 1, Iteration 1 playable skeleton (2026-10-13)

Built by: Muse subagent in the sandbox repo, against DESIGN_BIBLE.md.

### What was built
- `js/sim.js`: the whole simulation core as plain functions over a plain state object. It loads in the browser (window.AshesSim) and in node (module.exports), so the tests exercise the exact code the game runs.
  - 10 by 7 province grid, two fictional nations: The Vessari Compact (player, west) and The Khessite Dominion (AI, east). Capitals at the west and east ends of the middle row, marked, named (Vesskar City, Khessograd), and garrisoned.
  - Real-time tick: one tick is one day. Economy phase, AI phase, then movement and combat. Day counter and a campaign end at day 150.
  - Economy: steel income per owned province feeds a steel stockpile; factory levels consume steel daily and produce equipment; if steel runs short, factory levels sit idle and output drops. That is the resource gate, and a test proves it.
  - Units: Infantry Divisions and Drone Wings with strength, attack, defense. Click select, click an adjacent province to march or attack. Units sharing origin and target fight as one battle group. Provinces flip owner and color on capture.
  - Visible upgrade: build or upgrade a factory (levels 1 to 3) in any owned province; the on-map factory badge grows with level.
  - Research: Drone Gen 2 costs 60 research points and raises drone wings from attack 3 / defense 2 to attack 5 / defense 3. The unit panel and map chips show the live numbers, so the change is visible.
  - Win and lose: capture Khessograd to win, lose Vesskar City to lose, or reach day 150 with your capital standing for a survival victory.
  - Enemy AI: scripted and deliberately weak. It researches Gen 2 when it can, grows factories when rich, trains up to a 14 unit field army, and pushes west, refusing attacks it badly loses on paper.
- `index.html`, `css/style.css`, `js/main.js`: the browser layer. CSS grid map with owner colors, factory badges, unit chips; side panel with nation stats, province inspector, build and train buttons, research button, selected unit card, enemy summary, and a war log. Pause button and 1x / 2x speed buttons drive the tick timer. New Game starts a fresh random seed.
- `tests/sim.test.js`: 14 node tests covering game creation, tick, economy production, the steel gate, research accrual, battle resolution, province capture, order validation, factory build rules, the Drone Gen 2 stat change, capital capture victory, campaign end, and seed determinism.

### Test results
- `node --test tests/sim.test.js`: 14 pass, 0 fail.
- Headless autoplay smoke tests (scripted players):
  - Passive player (never acts): survives to day 151, survival victory. The AI expands but does not steamroll.
  - Sensible player (trains, researches, holds a capital garrison, advances in groups): survives to day 151 on 4 of 4 seeds, front stabilizes around the third column.
  - Reckless players who abandon the capital lane lose it in roughly 7 to 15 days. The capital fall is fast when the lane is left open; that is recorded in BACKLOG.md as a balance item, not hidden.

### Lessons burned into the code during this cycle
- Capital garrisons exist because the first smoke test ended with a lone enemy unit strolling down an empty middle row into an undefended capital on day 7.
- The AI has a 14 unit cap because the first uncapped run ended with a 51 unit pile-up that never attacked anything.
- Battle groups exist because single units attacking a pooled defending stack one at a time was guaranteed suicide, for the player and the AI alike. Smoke tests found it, the fix is grouped resolution.

### What is stubbed
Everything in BACKLOG.md. Short version: no fortifications, rail, navy, intel or fog, lore events, production line retooling, or drone cost-exchange scoring yet. Those are v1 systems from the bible and they are future cycles, listed openly in the backlog rather than faked here.

### Judge verdict
Not yet called for this cycle. Iteration 1 stands on the bible's own definition of done: running, playable end to end, tests green. The first Opus 5.5 judge pass should grade this skeleton before Iteration 2 scope is chosen.

## Cycle 2, Opus 5.5 judge pass on Iteration 1 (2026-10-13)

Judge: Claude Opus 5.5 at high, direct Anthropic line, graded against DESIGN_BIBLE.md with the cycle 1 summary and test results. Two calls: the main verdict (its tail was cut at the token cap) and a short completion call for the remainder. Verdict recorded here in substance.

### Verdict: PASS against the Iteration 1 bar
Every bar item confirmed: map and nations, day tick with pause and speeds, steel-gated economy, select/move/attack with battle groups, growing factory badge, Drone Gen 2 live stat change, win/lose/survival endings, 14 passing tests on a sim core shared by browser and tests, and an honest backlog. The judge called the multi-seed headless smoke runs "more rigor than the bar asked for."

### Two confirmations the judge demanded, both verified in code by Vector
- Day counter IS rendered (index.html day box; main.js updates it every render).
- Unit training DOES spend the equipment stockpile (trainUnit deducts CFG cost from nation equipment). The compounding loop's first link is intact.

### Compass check (judge's grades)
- HOI4 war heart: EMBRYO. Units, groups, captures exist. No production lines, no frontline concept, no supply, no retreat. "A board game of chips."
- Civ visible progression: EMBRYO. One badge grows. A day 140 map does not yet look like a different animal from day 1.
- EU5 lore: ABSENT. Syllable names, no events, no history, no grudges.
- Legibility: EMBRYO. Live chips and war log are good. Hidden rules will feel like bugs: the AI's private odds, first-unit damage soak, player-first resolution order.

### Risks named (accepted as the roadmap)
1. Grid coordinates as topology. Rail, rivers, coasts, crossings, blockade all need edge data. Move to an explicit province graph with typed edges now, while it is one file.
2. Units bought whole, priced in nothing. Production lines and the cost-exchange scoreboard both need units built from equipment over time, every asset carrying a cost. Later means touching combat, AI, and UI at once.
3. Hidden, order-dependent combat. Player-first resolution and damage soak are biases everything else will balance against. Fix before supply, terrain, and drones layer on. Combat odds must be one shared function the AI and the player preview both call.

### Next cycle prescribed by the judge (accepted as Cycle 3)
Rail is supply, legible on the map:
- Graph refactor: typed edges (land, river, coast). The CSS grid stays as a renderer. STOP computing adjacency from coordinates anywhere; delete the coordinate helpers.
- Rail: a buildable edge, costs steel, takes days to construct.
- Supply: a province is supplied if rail connects it to its capital within N hops through owned provinces. Out-of-supply units lose 10 percent attack and defense per day out (floor at 50 percent effectiveness), cannot reinforce, and after a 3-day grace take 2 percent strength attrition per day. Penalties are named modifiers in the combat math, shown on screen. Resupply clears penalties at the same 10 percent per day rate they accrued.
- Legibility: supply overlay (hatched red for unsupplied), rail drawn as track lines, construction dashed with days remaining, broken-supply marker with day count on unit counters, province hover or inspector shows the supply route and the break point, combat preview lists supply modifiers for both sides.
- Test: cutting one rail province flips a pocket to unsupplied; penalties verified after 1, 3, and 7 days.

### Sequencing note
Risk 2 (unit production over time and money costs) and the simultaneous-resolution half of risk 3 are real but come after Cycle 3. The shared odds function half of risk 3 rides along with Cycle 3 because supply modifiers must be visible to both sides.

## Cycle 4, Opus 5.5 judge pass on Cycle 3 (2026-10-13)

Verdict: PASS. All four prescribed items shipped and each closes the risk it targeted. The judge called the balance regression "good news" (it proved the old gate was hiding broken math) and the fixes the right kind: legible rules instead of hidden fudge.

- Rail conversion: KEEPER, in the judge's words, because it came out of balance pressure rather than wish-listing and directly expresses "rail is supply." Two conditions: keep it to one tunable number (it is: railConvertDays), and surface it in the attack preview (done in this cycle, below).
- Small flags, all fixed in this cycle: the inspector now shows hops as "N of 8 hops" against the limit; the attack preview warns how many rail edges a capture will start converting and that units beyond will be unsupplied; the Dominion's doctrine (1.5x superiority, never attacks out of supply, 10-day mobilization) is printed in its panel so its caution reads as rules, not randomness.
- Standing caveat: risk 3 is half closed. Odds are shared, but battles still resolve sequentially within a tick, so resolution order can matter. The judge's rider for a future cycle: compute all battle results from start-of-tick state, then apply.
- Next cycle prescribed: production lines and unit costs (risk 2). Lines assigned a template, steel cost per unit, build time in days, deployment at the capital, identical budgets for the AI, production panel with queue and steel drain, unit cost on the unit card, tests for budget parity, queue timing, and the rail-versus-units steel tradeoff. Exit criteria: passive falls in about 30 to 45 days, sensible survives 8 of 8. Deferred by the judge: fortifications, efficiency ramps, manpower, drones and EW, lore seed (lore waits until there are priced units and a real economy for it to describe).

## Cycle 5, production lines and unit costs, Step 1 of 4: sim (2026-10-13)

Prescription: Cycle 4 judge verdict (risk 2). This run did step 1 only, the simulation. Step 2 (production panel UI), step 3 (tests and balance), and step 4 (judge) remain for later runs of this loop.

### What was built
- Production lines in `js/sim.js`, same dual browser and node module pattern. Each nation starts with 2 lines, identical for player and AI: line 1 assigned infantry, line 2 assigned drone. A line holds a queue of orders (cap 9) and builds one unit at a time.
- Unit costs are now steel, paid over time instead of instantly: infantry costs 30 steel over 6 build days, a drone wing costs 15 steel over 3 build days. Both drain 5 steel per day while the line works, so every number stays whole and visible. Nothing is charged up front and no unit appears on the day it is ordered.
- A finished unit deploys at the nation's capital, for the player and the AI alike.
- Steel starvation is a rule, not a bug: if the stockpile cannot pay a line's daily drain, that line stalls for the day and makes no progress. Rail building (15 steel up front per edge) and unit production now compete for the same steel, which is the tradeoff the judge asked for.
- Retooling exists in the sim: `assignLineTemplate` switches a line's template and scraps the work in progress (steel already drained into it is lost); the queue count carries over. New API: `queueProduction`, `assignLineTemplate`, `productionPhase`, `productionDrain`, `queuedUnits`, `lineSteelPerDay`, `productionLine`.
- Instant purchases are gone. The old `trainUnit` survives only as a compatibility alias that queues an order on the first line assigned to that template, so the current browser UI keeps working until step 2 replaces the train buttons with the production panel. It spawns nothing and charges no equipment.
- Starting armies are unchanged in composition (5 infantry, 2 drone wings per side), so their repriced value is the same 180 the old equipment prices gave (5 times 30 plus 2 times 15), now denominated in steel paid over time for reinforcements. Starting steel, equipment, and research are unchanged.
- AI budget discipline fix, forced by the balance run below: the AI now grows a factory at most every 3 days and only with a steel stockpile of 60 or more. Same prices as the player, no discount; it is a spending rule for a scripted AI, like its attack doctrine.

### Test and balance results
- Existing suite: `node --test tests/sim.test.js`, 20 pass, 0 fail. (Formal production tests are step 3 of this cycle; the checks below are this step's verification, not a substitute.)
- Spot checks run by hand against the new API: player and AI lines, budgets, and costs are identical at game start; a queued infantry completes exactly on the 6th funded production day and deploys at the capital, with exactly 30 steel spent; with steel at zero a queued line makes zero progress and reports stalled; retooling zeroes progress.
- Passive player (never acts) across seeds 1, 7, 42, 99, 1234, 555, 2024, 31337: capital falls on day 36 on all 8 seeds, inside the judge's day 30 to 45 band and exactly matching the Cycle 3 measurement.
- Scripted sensible player (queues both lines, researches Drone Gen 2, builds rail toward unsupplied provinces with a steel buffer, masses every non-garrison unit at the easternmost capital-row province and attacks only eastward with a clear power edge): survives 8 of 8 seeds, all 8 by capturing the enemy capital between day 25 and day 78.

### Lessons from the balance run
- The first version of this step failed passively on 3 of 8 seeds (the player survived by doing nothing). Cause: the old AI grew a factory almost every day, each level adds daily steel demand, and with lines now also draining steel the Dominion's stockpile was pinned at zero by about day 25. Rail never got funded, its lead group starved at 50 percent penalty one province from the capital, and the AI's own rule against attacking while out of supply froze it there. Under instant purchases the AI won on day 36 before the spiral mattered. Pacing and steel-gating its factory growth (above) restored day 36 on all 8 seeds. The old instant-buy economy was hiding a factory steel spiral; production exposed it.
- A sensible player who leaves the starting units scattered in three provinces loses them piecemeal to the AI stack, production or not. Massing at one staging province is what survives; that matches the mission text for the step 3 script (trains, researches, rails unsupplied units, masses at the front).
- Equipment is now a factory-building currency only (see BACKLOG). Whether factories should also gate line count or build speed is flagged for the step 4 judge, not decided here.

## IRIS handover, lessons from the old PC loop (2026-10-13)

The old Ashes loop (Claude Code plus Hermes on Jash's PC, repo Ashes-Semantic-Zoom) is PAUSED by Jash's decision as of 2026-10-13 08:12: STOP file set, both scheduled tasks disabled, cycle 96 stopped mid-run with no commit. Head is cycle 95 (546b9ce), tests 233/233. This cloud build is the live Ashes work now. One dirty file on the PC branch (planning/gate-receipt.json) belongs to that repo, not this one. To resume the PC loop later, the STOP file comes out and the tasks re-enable; its Gate 3 spectator work and the old RTS demo design do not transfer as specs. The process lessons below do, and the loop treats them as binding.

- Jash's balance ruling (2026-10-11): both intended play paths must WIN through the public command path with at least 20 percent of starting friendly health left; a passive or reckless path must still lose. The old mission once "won" by 2.3 to 3.75 HP only because it was accidentally balanced around a bug (misplaced Fortify cover helping the player). Verify wins come from intended mechanics, never from a defect, and say so in the log if one does.
- Rebalance in small slices. A one-shot big rebalance regressed the old suite and was reverted; the fix was three small separately committed slices.
- Determinism and saves: the old sim produced a mission freeze at 3599.9s, time drift from per-frame rounding, and saves that soft-locked or failed to load. When save/load arrives in this build, it comes with save integrity and time-step determinism tests.
- Validate any scoring or judging metric before tuning against it. The old loop tuned cues against an unvalidated score and moved nothing.
- Commit discipline: commit every cycle that does not make tests worse; a cycle attempts the next slice instead of quitting.

## Cycle 5, production lines and unit costs, Step 4 of 4: balance ruling checks, fix, and judge (2026-10-13)

Prescription: Cycle 4 judge verdict (risk 2), step 4 of this cycle, plus the balance ruling checks that Step 3 predated. Steps 1 (sim, 8c40c9a), 2 (UI, 32368c0), and 3 (tests, b976a51) were done. This step closes the cycle. All code in this step was authored by Claude Opus 5.5 through the direct Anthropic line, per Jash's division of labor; the orchestrator wrote the briefs and the balance harness glue, applied the returns, ran every test and balance run itself, and verified the judge's factual claims by trace before accepting them.

### The ruling checks (Jash's ruling, quoted in the IRIS handover entry above, his words from 2026-10-11)
Both intended play paths must win through the public command path with at least 20 percent of starting friendly health left; a passive or reckless path must still lose. The harness is orchestrator glue, run on the 8 prescribed seeds (1, 7, 42, 99, 1234, 555, 2024, 31337). Starting friendly strength is 72 (5 infantry at 12 plus 2 drone wings at 6). Strength retention below is reported as end strength as a percent of that 72; end strength includes reinforcements built during the campaign, so values over 100 are growth, not retention in the strict sense (label corrected at the judge's direction). The scripts use only public commands: queueProduction, researchDroneGen2, buildRail, issueOrder. No state edits, no teleports, no direct province flips.
- Sensible player (queues both lines when idle, researches Drone Gen 2, builds rail to unsupplied provinces keeping a steel buffer, keeps 2 capital infantry as garrison, masses at the easternmost capital row province, attacks only eastward with 5 or more massed and a 1.5x stackPower edge): BEFORE the fix, wins 8 of 8, all by enemy capital capture on day 28, end strength 136.1 to 170.8 percent of starting. Check (b) passed before the fix and passes after it (below).
- Reckless player (abandons the capital lane: capital units vacate north and never return or defend; attacks piecemeal: exactly one field unit orders a move or attack per day; no rail discipline: buildRail is never called; it still queues production, so it is not a passive player in disguise): BEFORE the fix, reckless WON 5 of 8 seeds, capturing Khessograd on day 12 (seeds 1, 1234, 2024) and day 18 (seeds 7, 555), and lost on day 36 on the other 3. Check (a) FAILED.

### Root cause, verified by a day by day trace
The Dominion AI abandoned its own capital. In aiTakeTurn its capital units were grouped into origins like any province, and the no-attack fallback drifted them west on day 1, so Khessograd stood empty from day 2 except for fresh production deployments that also drifted west the next day. A lone walker down any row could take it unopposed. The backlog already admitted the AI never defended its capital on purpose; Iteration 1 taught this exact lesson for the player's capital and the AI side never got the same fix.

### The fix (one small slice, commit 96da531, built by Opus 5.5)
In aiTakeTurn, the first 3 idle Dominion units on its capital hold as a garrison and receive no orders; units beyond 3 act normally, so reinforcements still advance. The enemy panel doctrine text now states the garrison rule. No tuning numbers changed in this slice (the step 1 factory pacing change earlier in this cycle was a tuning change; the two facts are separate). Suite after the fix: 30 pass, 0 fail at that point.
- Opus usage, fix build call: [usage: in=18568, out=1429]. One call, no fix rounds. The same spec was validated in a throwaway prototype by the orchestrator before the brief was sent, and the returned code matched the prototype's semantics exactly.

### Balance after the fix (orchestrator rerun, all 8 seeds)
- Passive player: capital falls on day 36 on all 8 seeds, unchanged, inside the 30 to 45 band.
- Sensible player: wins 8 of 8, all by enemy capital capture, on days 43 to 52 (per seed: 47, 50, 47, 43, 49, 46, 46, 52). End strength as percent of starting 72: 95.8, 120.8, 81.9, 118.1, 130.6, 108.3, 93.1, 144.4. The 20 percent floor clears on every seed through real orders only. Extra honesty check run by the orchestrator: counting only surviving units of the original starting army, strength left is 24 on every seed (33.3 percent of 72, the untouched 2 infantry capital garrison), so the floor clears even with reinforcements excluded.
- Reckless player: LOSES 8 of 8. Its capital falls on day 36 on 6 seeds and on day 54 on seeds 7 and 555. Both ruling checks now PASS.

### Judge verdict (fresh Opus 5.5 call, not the builder context)
- Opus usage, judge call: [usage: in=6437, out=8127].
- VERDICT: PASS, conditional on the fix-now flags below (all closed in this step, see next section). Every prescribed deliverable shipped and both exit criteria met. The judge's deciding reason: the cycle found its own failure in the reckless check, traced it to a real AI defect, fixed it with one small rule change and no tuning edits, and re-verified all three player profiles.
- Compass check: HOI4 war heart FORMING (above embryo; production, retooling, drain, rail competition, capital deployment form a real supply to front chain; fortifications, frontline bending, simultaneous combat still missing). Civ visible progression EMBRYO (nothing this cycle makes a year 3 map look different from year 1). EU5 lore ABSENT (names only; the judge called this a debt, not a deferral, five cycles in). Legibility EMBRYO, trending up (panel states its rules and flags stalls; no tooltips, no order arrows, and at verdict time the panel had never been seen in a real browser).
- Ruling on the open equipment question: factories must gate production line COUNT, not build speed, and equipment as a factory only currency is acceptable for exactly one more cycle, not as the end state, because the bible's compounding loop (factories feed production, production feeds the army) is currently closed on itself. Line count is legible; speed modifiers are the Stellaris trap. Thresholds are loop tuning; whether a locked slot feels good is taste and is parked for Jash in DECISIONS_FOR_JASH.md.
- Next prescription (Cycle 6, "Close the loop, fix the clock"): (A) factories gate line count, start unchanged at 2 lines, extra slots unlock at loop-chosen total factory level thresholds, hard cap 4, identical rule for the AI, locked slots shown in the panel with the exact unlock condition in plain words, tests for slot count, locked queue rejection, and parity. (B) Simultaneous battle resolution from start-of-tick state (closes the Cycle 4 risk 3 caveat), including units swapping provinces across the same edge meeting in battle instead of passing through, with order-reversal and edge-swap tests. Exit criteria: full suite green, balance rerun on all 8 seeds (passive 30 to 45, sensible 8 of 8 above the 20 percent floor, reckless loses 8 of 8, sensible shown using the factory to line path in at least one seed trace), a real browser render check of the locked slot UI, and log and backlog updated with no contradictions. Deferred in stated order: lore seed is reserved as Cycle 7 and not to be bumped again (written backstories for both nations, a codex panel, 3 event cards, tone and content to Jash for approval), then fortifications, efficiency ramps, manpower, drones and EW, the cost-exchange scoreboard, intel and fog, navy.

### The judge's claims check, verified by the orchestrator before acceptance
1. "Passive day 36 unchanged is doubtful; a held garrison should shrink the attacking force." VERIFIED TRUE and explained. Trace of passive seed 1 after the fix: the garrison units (ids 12, 13, 14, the starting capital stack) never left Khessograd on any day. The stack standing on the player capital at the fall was ids 11, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20: a starting front drone plus production deployments that were beyond the garrison count when they left. The front army plus excess reinforcements were always sufficient; the day never moved.
2. "Reckless surviving to day 54 on seeds 7 and 555 is counterintuitive; show a trace." TRACED. On seed 7 the Dominion's westernmost unit was still at x=5 on day 12 and x=4 on day 30, reaching x=1 only on day 48; on seed 1 it reached x=4 by day 12 and x=1 by day 30. The piecemeal attacks on seed 7 kept meeting Dominion groups further east, so the advance west was slower even though the reckless capital lane stood open. The loss is real, only later.
3. "Factory steel spiral conflicts with equipment funds factories." RESOLVED, no conflict. ## Cycle 6, Close the loop, fix the clock, Step 2 of 5: simultaneous battles, sim (2026-10-13)

Prescription: Cycle 5 judge verdict, item (B), closing the Cycle 4 caveat that battles resolved sequentially within a tick with the player first. This run did step 2 only. Step 3 (locked slot UI), step 4 (tests and balance), and step 5 (judge) remain. Note on process: the 12:43 run of this step was interrupted and committed nothing; this run is its relaunch, verified against a clean tree with HEAD still at step 1 (fa9dfeb) before any work. All code in this step was authored by Claude Opus 5.5 through the direct Anthropic line (5 anchor replacement blocks, applied verbatim by the orchestrator); the orchestrator wrote the brief, ran every check itself, and verified the behaviors below with its own scenario harness.

### What Opus built
- `js/sim.js`: a new exported movementPhase(state) replaces the sequential group execution in tick (the player-first sort and executeGroup are gone). It snapshots every ordered unit's origin and target, builds groups keyed nation, origin, target, and assigns each unit to at most one engagement per tick, in this priority: (a) edge swap meeting battles, opposing groups crossing the same edge in opposite directions; (b) province battles, where all snapshot occupants of a target province defend it even if they had orders elsewhere (their orders are cancelled for the tick), and all attacking groups against one province combine into one battle; (c) incoming clashes, opposing groups converging on the same empty province; (d) unopposed moves.
- Every engagement is computed on shallow unit copies from the snapshot (real units are untouched while any battle is calculated), with clone lists sorted by unit id and its own rng seeded deterministically from the game seed, the tick count, and a canonical engagement key, so an engagement's rolls do not depend on other engagements or on unit order. Meeting battles are symmetric: both sides deal damage with their attack power. Province battles keep the existing math exactly (attack versus defense, 12 round cap, damage soak in unit id order). Results are then applied at once: winners march in only if no living enemy unit is staying at their target, captures flip owners and run the capital check in canonical province order, and every order touched by the phase is cleared. The exported resolveBattle keeps its signature and behavior for existing callers.
- `js/main.js`: the attack preview keeps its province battle line unchanged and adds, per defended neighbor, the honest meeting line: "If they march out and meet you on the road: your attack N vs their attack M." Nothing else in the UI changed.

### Opus usage
- First build call: [usage: in=28017, out=16000]. It returned NO text: the entire 16000 output tokens were spent before any block was emitted (adaptive thinking consumed the cap). Recorded as spend, retried once per the mission's failure rule with a 32000 cap and an output economy instruction.
- Retry build call: [usage: in=28114, out=23556]. Five blocks, all anchors matched exactly once, applied cleanly.
- Step total: in=56131, out=39556. Cycle 6 running total: in=73791, out=44150. Recorded grand total across cycles (sum of the usage lines in this log; Cycle 5 step 1 and the Cycle 2 judge calls were never recorded, so the true total is higher): in=143716, out=101976.

### Test and verification results (run by the orchestrator)
- `node --check js/sim.js` and `node --check js/main.js`: pass. Em dash scan of both files: zero.
- `node --test tests/sim.test.js`: 32 pass, 0 fail (suite unchanged this step; the formal simultaneous resolution tests are step 4).
- Order reversal determinism: a busy movement phase (two player groups attacking and moving, three enemy groups moving, one defender group ordered away from an attacked province) run on two identical states, one with state.units reversed, produces identical results: same units, positions, strengths, owners, and game over state. PASS.
- Edge swap: an isolated player infantry at p4_3 and enemy infantry at p5_3 ordered across the same edge at each other did NOT pass through. They met on the road (log: "Vessari and Khessite columns meet on the road between Belfeld and Ashmund. The Vessari win and march on to Ashmund."), the enemy infantry was destroyed, and the player survivor (strength 2) marched on and took its target. PASS.
- Defender drawn into defense: both enemy units at p5_3 were ordered north to p5_2 while a player stack attacked p5_3; neither marched away, both fought as defenders from the snapshot and died there. PASS.
- Balance anchor (full passive games, all 8 standard seeds): the player capital falls on day 36 on every seed, exactly the Cycle 5 measurement, so removing player-first resolution did not shift the passive band. The sensible and reckless reruns belong to step 4.

### Lessons
- Output caps are a real build risk with this model: a 16000 token cap produced zero usable text on a brief whose answer needed about 21000 characters. Build calls for whole phase rewrites should start at 32000, and the wasted call still counts in the usage ledger above.
- The one engagement per unit rule is what makes simultaneity tractable: assignment priority (road first, then province defense, then clashes) removes the double fighting and pass-through cases by construction, and per engagement rng seeds make order independence provable rather than hoped for.

### The one visible number, chosen and logged before any balance run
- Efficiency affects BUILD DAYS ONLY: how many funded days a unit takes to build. The steel drain per day (5 steel for both templates) and the listed steel cost of a unit (CFG steelCost, 30 infantry and 15 drone) never change; a practiced line finishes sooner and therefore stops draining sooner, which is the same single effect seen from the wallet side, not a second bonus.
- Why not the steel drain per day: the base drain is 5, so an integer drain can only move in steps of a whole steel, a 20 percent jump per step, far too coarse for a ramp that should be felt gradually, and a changing drain would conflate line experience with a price discount on a cost the panel and the unit card quote as fixed. Work points give the ramp fine integer grain instead: a unit needs buildDays times 100 work points (infantry 600, drone 300), and a funded day adds the line's efficiency percent as work points, so every percent is a whole point and the only division anywhere is the stated ceiling in the readout for a fresh unit's effective days.
- Tuning, one CFG number per parameter, stated in advance: lineEfficiencyFloor 100 (a fresh line builds at exactly the speed every earlier cycle balanced against, so the ramp is a gain from the baseline and never a hidden nerf to a new line), lineEfficiencyRisePerDay 2 (the cap is reached after 25 funded working days, inside a campaign but not in its first week), lineEfficiencyCap 150 (at the cap, infantry completes in exactly 4 funded days and a drone in exactly 2, because 4 times 150 is 600 and 2 times 150 is 300). Retool rule, stated in advance: efficiency drops all the way to the floor, on top of the existing scrap of work in progress (work and progressDays zeroed, no steel refund, as before).

### What was built (commit 7332c9f)
- js/sim.js only. Line objects gain efficiency (starting at the floor) and work (work points on the current unit), in makeProductionLines and in the lines syncProductionLines opens later, so a line earned at 16 factory levels starts at the floor like any other. A line object staged without the new fields reads as a fresh line at the floor, and productionPhase normalizes missing fields before use.
- The readout, beside lineSteelPerDay as prescribed: lineEfficiency (the line's percent, the floor when absent), productionWorkNeeded (buildDays times 100), lineWorkPerDay (the efficiency itself), lineBuildDays (the ceiling of need over work per day: funded days a fresh unit would take at the line's current efficiency), and lineDaysLeft (the same ceiling over the work remaining on the unit in progress, zero when nothing is queued). All five are exported. productionPhase builds with them: a funded day pays the unchanged drain, adds lineWorkPerDay of work, then raises efficiency by the rise toward the cap (the rise applies from the next day, so a day's work is always at the efficiency the day started with), and completes the unit when work reaches productionWorkNeeded; work past the need on the finishing day is lost, the same shape as the part day progressDays always discarded. A stalled day adds no work and no efficiency and spends nothing, as before. queueProduction, the ordering path the player and the AI share, now reports and logs its build days from lineBuildDays, so an order placed on a practiced line quotes the ramped days; at the floor that is the base 6 and 3, unchanged.
- progressDays keeps its exact meaning (funded days spent on the current unit, reset on completion and on retool), which is why the whole existing suite passes unmodified (see results). The panel does not read the new fields yet; that is step 2, and the backlog records the one place the panel's base day count can read a day stale on a ramped line until then.

### The judge's Flag 1, verified by the builder before acceptance, carried to Cycle 10 step 0
- Flag 1: in the 116 to 119 percent band, a fresh infantry quote overstates the charge by one day (and, following from the day, by 5 steel). Code evidence, verified by the builder in this run's own probe and reads: js/sim.js documents lineBuildDays as the funded days a fresh unit would take if the efficiency never moved during the build, and says the real build can only be this or faster (the comment above lineBuildDays); lineBuildDays returns the ceiling of productionWorkNeeded over lineWorkPerDay at the starting efficiency, while productionPhase adds the rising efficiency day by day. The builder's probe, charging through productionPhase at each staged efficiency: 114 percent quotes 6 and charges 6 days for 30 steel; 115 quotes 6, charges 6 and 30; 116, 117, 118, and 119 each quote 6 and charge 5 days for 25 steel; 120 quotes 5 and charges 5 and 25, because the ceiling itself drops there. The band is infantry only: a drone at 118 percent still reads 3, because its rising work passes its 300 need only on the third day. On screen, js/main.js's efficiency row states the ceiling as plain fact ("a fresh unit takes N days here instead of the base M days"), so at 118 percent it reads 6 against a base of 6, hiding a real gain, while the actual charge is 5 days and 25 steel; queueProduction's log line quotes the listed steel over lineBuildDays with no qualifier. Test 5 pins the ceiling invariant (never longer than the readout) rather than equality, which is how the inaccuracy is currently locked in.
- The judge's ruling on the step 3 finding, accepted: acceptable as a mechanism, not acceptable as an on screen quote. Not a fail, because the fail condition is about computation paths and there is no path around the readout; the discrepancy is between a static ceiling and the dynamic process inside the one function, the quote never understates, and no player is ever charged more than quoted. Not merely acceptable legibility, because the excusing semantics live in a code comment the player never sees, one surface states the number as fact, and the bible's legibility bar plus the Cycle 8 judge's grading of a smaller inaccuracy (a badge hidden while the correct facts sat on the card) put a wrong live number that is cheap to make exact in the fix-now class.
- The prescribed fix, assigned to Cycle 10 step 0, recorded here in full so step 0 does not re-derive it: in js/sim.js only, make both readout day functions exact by iterating the documented rise, in integer arithmetic, with no signature or export changes. lineBuildDays: starting from the line's current efficiency as work per day and accumulated work 0, count funded days, adding the current work per day each day and then raising it by CFG.lineEfficiencyRisePerDay toward and not past CFG.lineEfficiencyCap, until the accumulated work reaches productionWorkNeeded; return that count. lineDaysLeft: the same iteration against the work remaining, starting from the line's current efficiency. productionPhase is not touched: the fix makes the quote match the existing charge, not the other way around. The sim comment is updated so the readout is described as exact in funded days, and the BACKLOG.md wording describing the readout as a ceiling is updated in the same step.
- Exit criteria for Cycle 10 step 0, all required, as prescribed: (1) the band case explicit and green: infantry staged at 118 percent returns lineBuildDays 5, queueProduction reports buildDays 5, and productionPhase charges 5 funded days and 25 steel. (2) Test 5 repinned from the ceiling invariant to equality: for every efficiency from 100 to 150, for both templates, the days charged through productionPhase equal lineBuildDays, and at least one in progress lineDaysLeft case in the band is pinned equal to the funded days actually remaining; full suite passes, count recorded (expected 65 if the repin edits existing tests, more if a test is added). (3) The staged values the browser check relies on verified unchanged under the exact readout: floor infantry 6 and drone 3; 130 percent infantry 5 and drone 3; cap infantry 4 and drone 2. (4) Balance rerun byte identical to tools/baseline-cycle9.txt. (5) Browser checks: efficiency 15 of 15, fort 17 of 17, lore 34 of 34, browser 6 of 6; node check clean; dash byte scan zero. (6) CYCLE_LOG.md and BACKLOG.md record the semantics change in the step 0 entry.
- No other fix-now flags. The judge looked for and did not find: a second efficiency computation anywhere, a drain or listed cost that moves with efficiency, the AI rising or being charged on different numbers, a retool path that drops efficiency without scrapping work or scraps work without dropping efficiency, a stalled or idle day earning efficiency, efficiency passing the cap, or any contradiction between this log, BACKLOG.md, and DECISIONS_FOR_JASH.md on Cycle 9 numbers.

### Cycle 10 prescription from the judge, accepted and logged here
Cycle 10, the second lore pass, in the deferred order the Cycle 8 judge set, placed immediately after Cycle 9 so it is not bumped a second time. Its two contents, recorded side by side in that order: recurring event texture, and the capital endpoint wording. All text is loop written and flagged prominently for Jash under the lore rule, in DECISIONS_FOR_JASH.md and in the log, open for his rewrite or veto, and the loop does not stall waiting for his approval. No mechanical effect of any kind, unless Jash rules otherwise on DECISIONS_FOR_JASH.md item 11 before the step that would build it; absent such a ruling, every card prints the existing no effect sentence and means it.
- Step 0: close Flag 1 above, with its exact fix and six exit criteria.
- Step 1, content and recording hooks: draft the recurring event texture in js/lore.js and the capital endpoint wording, and add any recording hooks the texture needs in js/sim.js. Recurring texture cards fire on stated, deterministic, repeatable campaign facts (the builder chooses the facts from events the sim already produces, for example a rail line completed or a captured rail conversion finished, a fortification completed, a province retaken after changing hands, a production line reaching full efficiency), each card carries a plain words trigger line, ships only the variants (player, enemy, both, or a neutral text where sides do not apply) that real campaigns can produce, and prints the no effect sentence. Occurrences are recorded in state (what fired, on which day, for which side, and how many times) by a recording phase in the Cycle 7 beatPhase pattern, and no rule, price, odds estimate, or AI decision reads those records. The capital endpoint wording: both capital codex entries (Vesskar City and Khessograd) are extended so each describes both endings the sim has, the capital falling and the day 150 survival ending, in wording consistent with the sim's own end texts, closing the gap recorded in DECISIONS_FOR_JASH.md item 9 and BACKLOG.md. Exit criteria: node check clean and dash scan zero on all copy; a reachability tally run on real campaign profiles on the standard seeds (passive and sensible at minimum), recorded in the log with its profile scope named, proving every shipped variant can fire and every recurring trigger fires at least twice in at least one tallied campaign; the full balance rerun byte identical to tools/baseline-cycle9.txt; the new content listed item by item in the DECISIONS_FOR_JASH.md lore flag at the top of that file in this same step.
- Step 2, UI: recurring cards surface through the existing event card overlay and its queue, with the occurrence count or day shown honestly on repeat firings, and the codex shows the recurring texture reached so far (with counts and days) alongside the turning points, in the existing codex structure. ### Choosing the facts: a prototype tally before any text was written
- The three shipped facts were chosen from data, not from the prescription's example list alone. A scratch copy of the repo in /tmp carried prototype hooks for seven candidate facts the sim already produces, and all four harness profiles (passive, sensible, reckless, fortress) ran on the 8 standard seeds, 32 campaigns. Results per candidate, totals across each profile's 8 campaigns: a province retaken after changing hands fired 0 times in all 32 campaigns (unreachable in current play; not shipped, and recorded here and in BACKLOG.md rather than silently dropped). New rail completed fired up to 23 times in one sensible campaign (184 player occurrences across 8 sensible campaigns), a province captured up to 13 times in one passive campaign, and a unit completed up to 40 times in one campaign: all three fire reliably, but at that frequency, under a hard pausing card overlay (step 2's prescribed surface), they would be noise, not texture, so they were not shipped either; the builder records them as available facts if a future non pausing surface ever wants them. The three shipped facts are the ones that are both reachable and occasional: a fortification level completed, a captured rail conversion finished, and a production line reaching full efficiency.
- One design consequence of the event shapes: the beats could be recorded by an end of tick phase because their facts persist as predicates (an owner differs, a flag is set, a line count holds). These three facts are transient (a build finishing, a conversion completing, an efficiency value crossing its cap on one funded day), so no end of tick predicate can count them exactly. They are therefore recorded at the moment they happen, in constructionPhase and productionPhase, through one helper in the beatPhase pattern: recordTexture only appends to state.textures, gated by CFG.campaignTextures in the CFG.campaignBeats pattern, and nothing reads the records. The step 3 prescription's zero effect test shape (recording disabled, campaigns identical except the records) was spot checked by the builder this step and holds (below).

### Lessons
- Reachability and frequency are both shipping criteria for recurring content, and only a tally measures either: the most narratively obvious candidate (a province retaken) fired zero times in 32 campaigns, and the most available ones (rail built, provinces captured, units completed) fired so often they would have drowned the cards they were meant to texture. The prototype cost one scratch run and decided the whole content set.
- Transient facts cannot be recorded by an end of tick predicate phase; they must be recorded where they happen. The discipline that makes that safe is the same one beatPhase has: one helper, one state field, a CFG off switch in the established pattern, and a grep proving no rule reads the field.
- Profile scope honesty cuts both ways: the tally's minimum scope (passive and sensible) proved five of the six shipped variants, and the sixth (player walls) is proven by the fortress profile that exists precisely to build them. Naming which profile proves which variant is what keeps a true claim from reading as a broader one.

### Cycle 11 prescription from the judge, accepted and logged here
Cycle 11 is Manpower, next in the deferred order the Cycle 8 judge set (after Cycle 10: manpower, then drones and EW with the cost exchange scoreboard, then intel and fog, then navy). No carried flag exists, so Cycle 11 has no step 0; it starts at step 1. The judge's framing: manpower must complete the bible's compounding loop in its plain form (factories feed production, production feeds the army, and the army is fed by people the ground provides), so ground held must be what raises an army, and raising an army must be able to run out.
- Step 1, sim: one manpower pool per nation in state, governed by one CFG number per parameter (the efficiency pattern): a starting pool, a daily intake per owned province (captured ground raises intake, lost ground lowers it), and a manpower cost per unit template paid from the pool. Costs are loop tuning, but the shape is prescribed: infantry costs substantially; a drone wing costs a small crew cost, not zero (zero would make drones a manpower bypass and pre decide the Cycle 12 cost exchange balance). Payment timing: paid in full at queue time through queueProduction, the one ordering path both nations share, because no queue cancel exists to refund through; a queue attempt the pool cannot pay is rejected with { ok: false } and a legible reason carrying the real numbers (cost, pool, shortfall), exactly as locked lines reject today, and nothing is queued or charged. No other rule reads the pool except the queue gate and its readouts: combat, supply, odds, prices in steel and equipment, and AI movement are untouched by it. The Dominion AI queues through the identical queueProduction path and is bound by the identical pool, intake, and costs; any pacing rule it needs is a spending rule like its factory pacing, stated in the log, never a discount. Shared readouts are exported in the readout family pattern (current pool, daily intake, per template manpower cost), and every quoted or charged manpower number anywhere traces to them. Exit criteria: node check clean, dash scan zero, existing suite green unmodified except where a test legitimately pins old queue behavior, and spot checks showing accrual over days, queue deduction, rejection at insufficient pool with correct numbers, and AI parity in isolation.
- Step 2, UI: manpower legible at the moment of use. The nation card shows the pool, the daily intake, and what intake depends on (provinces held) in plain words. The production panel shows each template's manpower cost beside its steel cost and build days, the pool the queue would draw from, and a rejected queue attempt surfaces its reason visibly. The unit card cost line gains the manpower cost. The enemy card shows the Dominion's pool and intake by the same numbers, as judge flag 4 did for factories, so the constraint reads as a shared rule, not a player tax. Exit criteria: a browser check (new tools file or an extension of an existing one, established pattern) asserting the pool and intake on the nation card, the manpower cost on a production row and on the unit card, and a visible rejection when the pool is staged short, with expectations computed from the sim readouts and CFG, not hardcoded; all prior browser checks still pass; no horizontal scroll at 390 px.
- Step 3, tests and balance: formal tests pinning accrual (intake sums over owned provinces, rises on capture, falls on loss, identical formula for both nations); payment (an infantry order deducts exactly its CFG cost at queue time, a drone order its crew cost, a rejected order deducts nothing and queues nothing); the gate (queueing beyond the pool fails with the numbered reason, and topping the pool up by exactly the shortfall makes the same order succeed); AI parity through the real tick path (the Cycle 9 parity test pattern); and one non vacuity mutant shown failing exactly its target test (for example intake computed only for the player, failing only the parity test, counts recorded). The constraint must be proven to bind, not merely to exist: at least one recorded trace on a standard seed, through public commands only, where a queue attempt is actually rejected for manpower or a profile's build rhythm is measurably manpower limited, while the ruling profiles still meet their bands; a manpower system that never binds on any profile is decoration and fails this step. Balance: the full rerun on the 8 standard seeds against Jash's ruling, which is the exit bar, not byte identity (manpower is a real mechanic, so numbers will move; movement is reported per seed and per profile against the Cycle 9 baseline): passive capital falls on day 30 to 45 on all 8 seeds; sensible wins 8 of 8 through the public command path with at least 20 percent of starting strength left, reported both with reinforcements counted and counting only surviving starting units; reckless loses 8 of 8. Any broken band is fixed by one small tuning slice at a time (one CFG number or one pacing rule per commit), never a one shot rebalance, and wins must come from intended mechanics, never from a defect. A new committed baseline, tools/baseline-cycle11.txt, in the harness's own format. BACKLOG.md and DECISIONS_FOR_JASH.md updated with no contradictions.
- Step 4, judge: a fresh judge with no builder context, grading against the bible and this prescription, independently rerunning the suite, the balance rerun against the ruling bands and the new baseline, and all browser checks, verifying in code that every manpower number traces to the shared readouts and that the AI lives under the identical gate, and reproducing the binding trace and the non vacuity mutant. A pass requires the constraint demonstrably binding, parity proven, and every ruling band met.
- Taste parked for Jash by the judge, not decided by the prescription: whether manpower should also gate factory or fortification construction crews; whether the pool should have a cap that wastes overflow intake; the flavor name of the intake, if any, beyond the plain word manpower; and whether a future cycle may spend manpower on partial unit reinforcement (today there is none, and Cycle 11 does not add it). Thresholds, intake rate, starting pool, and per template costs are loop tuning under the bands above.

### Tuning chosen by the loop (recorded per the prescription)
- CFG.manpowerStart 1200, CFG.manpowerPerProvincePerDay 1, and manpowerCost on CFG.unitTypes beside the steel costs: infantry 120, drone 25.
- Why these numbers: each nation owns 35 provinces at the start, so intake starts at 35 per day for both. The harness rhythm of one order per line at a time spends manpower at the completion rhythm, about 34 per day for the two starting lines (an infantry every 5 to 6 funded days at 120, a drone wing every 2 to 3 at 25), so the first two lines roughly break even against intake and the starting pool is a real reserve, not decoration: opening lines 3 and 4, or queueing ahead of the lines instead of one order at a time, spends faster than intake and draws the pool down, which is the pressure the step 3 binding trace will measure. The starting pool's floor was set by the existing suite, not by feel: the queue cap test queues 9 infantry orders and then a drone order on a fresh game with no intake in between (9 times 120 plus 25 is 1105), so a pool under 1105 would have broken a test that pins queue capacity, not manpower; 1200 clears it with 95 to spare, and the suite below is green with no test modified.

### What was built (commit c59a3fd)
- js/sim.js only. Each nation's state gains manpower, starting at CFG.manpowerStart for both nations in createGame.
- Readouts, exported in the readout family pattern: manpowerCost(template) reads the CFG cost, manpowerPool(state, nationId) reads the current pool (a nation staged without the field reads as a fresh pool at the start value), and manpowerIntake(state, nationId) is the owned province count times CFG.manpowerPerProvincePerDay, so captured ground raises intake and lost ground lowers it by the same formula for both nations.
- incomePhase accrues the intake beside steel and research, for both nations through the same call, so the tick and economyTick both feed the pool. That is the only accrual site.
- queueProduction is the gate: after the locked line and queue full checks (whose order and reasons are unchanged), it checks the pool through a manpower refusal helper in the locked line pattern. A short pool returns { ok: false, manpower: true, template, manpowerCost, current, missing } with the reason "Not enough manpower to queue a Infantry Division. It costs 120 manpower, you have 119, you are 1 short." (numbers are the run's own), and queues, charges, and logs nothing. A paid order deducts the full cost at queue time, the success result gains a manpowerCost field beside the unchanged steel cost field, the trainUnit alias passes it through, and the queue log line now states the manpower paid beside the steel and days.
- Retool settlement, one addition the prescription's shape forced: queued orders were paid for the old template and the queue count carries over a retool, so assignLineTemplate settles the manpower difference for every queued order before switching (a dearer template charges the difference per queued order and the retool is rejected with a numbered reason, changing nothing, when the pool is short; a cheaper template refunds the difference). Without this, queueing drone wings at 25 and retooling the line would field infantry at the crew price, a manpower bypass of exactly the kind the prescription's not zero drone cost exists to prevent. Steel on a retool is untouched: work in progress and its drained steel stay scrapped, exactly as the pinned retool test states.
- Nothing else reads the pool: grep of js/sim.js shows manpower only in the CFG entries, the header note, the readout family, the queue gate, the retool settlement, the createGame initializers, incomePhase, the trainUnit passthrough, and the exports. Combat, supply, odds, steel and equipment prices, and AI movement are untouched, and the AI needed no pacing change: it already queues only through queueProduction, one order per idle line, so the identical gate binds it with no discount and no new rule.

### Lessons
- A paid at queue time resource and a carried queue make retool a pricing surface whether the prescription names it or not: any system that charges at order time must decide what a template switch does to orders already paid for, in the same step that introduces the charge, or it ships a discount path no test will catch because every retool test predates the charge. The settlement shape chosen here (settle the difference per queued order, reject when short) is the smallest rule that keeps one price per unit.
- The existing suite can bound a new resource's starting stock exactly the way it bounded the efficiency ramp's rise: the queue cap test, written two cycles before manpower existed, silently required a starting pool of at least 1105. Reading the suite as a set of constraints on the tuning, before choosing numbers, is what let this step ship with zero tests modified.

### Binding trace (recorded this run, seed 42, public commands only)
- Queueing ahead, the play pattern the harness profiles do not use: line 1 is filled to its queue cap with 9 infantry orders (9 times 120 is 1080), then drone wings are queued on line 2. Exactly 13 orders are paid in total (1080 plus 4 times 25 is 1180 of the 1200 starting pool), and the 14th attempt, a fifth drone wing, is rejected for manpower alone: ok false, manpower true, template drone, cost 25, current 20, missing 5, reason "Not enough manpower to queue a Drone Wing. It costs 25 manpower, you have 20, you are 5 short." The queues stand at 9 and 4; line 2 still has queue room and steel is never charged at queue time, so the pool is the only gate that refused. The constraint binds, proven on a standard seed through queueProduction only, and the trace is pinned by test 5 above.
- Honest scope, recorded rather than smoothed: the harness profiles themselves never bind. In passive campaigns the Dominion's pool dips to a minimum of 1090 early and ends at 2135, identical on all 8 seeds (the scripted profiles dominate seed variation, as in step 1), and no harness order in any profile was gated, because the profiles' one order per line at a time rhythm spends about what intake earns (about 34 per day against 35). Manpower at the chosen tuning is a reserve and expansion constraint: it binds a player who queues ahead or expands lines faster than intake, not the measured harness rhythm. No tuning slice was made to force profile binding: no ruling band broke, and tightening the numbers until the profiles bind would have been a rebalance in search of a trace, not a fix for a broken band.

### Lessons
- A parity mutant fails exactly one test only if the rest of the section is shaped around it: the accrual test deliberately pins the Dominion's intake through the shared readout, not through incomePhase, so the intake only for the player mutant has exactly one pin to break, the tick parity test. Designing the mutant and the test split together, before writing either, is what makes the recorded count (79 pass, 1 fail) evidence rather than luck.
- A mechanic can bind honestly and still never bind in the harness profiles: the profiles order one unit per line at a time, which spends manpower at almost exactly the intake rate, so three cycles of balance reruns are byte identical while a queue ahead player is refused on the 14th order. The binding trace has to use a play pattern the profiles do not, and the log has to say the profiles do not bind, instead of tuning the numbers until they do.

### Cycle 12 prescription from the judge, accepted and logged here
Cycle 12 is Drones and EW, with the cost exchange scoreboard, next in the deferred order the Cycle 8 judge set (after Cycle 12: intel and fog, then navy). No carried flag exists, so Cycle 12 has no step 0; it starts at step 1. The judge's honest statement of the current state, verified in code: research has exactly one item, Drone Gen 2 (flat researchPerDay 3 for both nations, cost 60 points, the AI decision made at the start of the tick on start of day numbers), raising drone wings from attack 3 and defense 2 to attack 5 and defense 3; a drone wing is an ordinary unit template (strength 6, 15 steel over 3 build days, 25 manpower) fighting inside stack combat like infantry; there is no interceptor, no jamming or EW mechanic, no air specific combat step, and no cost exchange record anywhere in the sim, UI, or lore. The bible's signature mechanic is therefore entirely unbuilt: a cheap drone forcing an expensive interceptor launch is a victory even when the drone dies, the scoreboard tracks who bleeds money faster, and drone generations and jamming generations counter each other through research. The cycle's one visible number: drone effectiveness percent in battle, a single percent computed by one shared readout from the two generation numbers, used identically by the battle, the attack preview, the stackPower estimate the AI decides with, and every on screen quote. The scoreboard's one headline number: net exchange in steel, value you destroyed or forced the enemy to spend, minus value you lost or were forced to spend.
- Step 1, sim: interceptor launches, the exchange ledger, and the EW generation counter. Interceptor stock, one shared path: each nation holds an interceptor stockpile in state, starting at a loop tuned CFG number, replenished only through a priced production path the loop chooses and records (a third production template whose completion adds to the stockpile instead of deploying a map unit, or a queueProduction priced stock order are both acceptable shapes; an instant free or steel only at click purchase that bypasses the production and manpower discipline of the existing economy is not). Interceptors carry one CFG steel cost, and the tuning shape is prescribed: one interceptor's full cost (steel, plus manpower if the chosen path charges it) must exceed one drone wing's full cost (15 steel, 25 manpower) by a wide, stated margin, because the exchange asymmetry is the mechanic; the exact multiple is loop tuning, recorded in the log with the arithmetic shown. The launch rule, inside the shared combat path and nowhere else: when a battle is fought in which the attacking side fields at least one drone wing, the defending nation automatically launches interceptors, one per attacking drone wing, up to its stock on hand; each launch consumes one interceptor, is valued at the interceptor's CFG cost in the ledger, and destroys its target drone wing outright, removed before or as the battle resolves by a stated, deterministic rule the step's tests can pin (the drone dies to the interceptor, not to battle damage, and is never counted twice). No drones in the attack means no launches, ever; a defender with zero stock launches nothing and the battle proceeds exactly as today. Whether the drone's own attack still counts in the round it dies is a sim shape decision the loop makes, states in the log, and pins in a test; it must be the same rule for both nations and visible in the preview (step 2). Launching is automatic in this cycle: a player toggle is taste, parked below, not built. The exchange ledger, record only: state gains a per nation exchange record, accrued at the moment each fact happens, in the beats and textures recording pattern: steel value of enemy units destroyed by your forces, steel value of your units the enemy destroyed, steel value of interceptor launches you forced the enemy to make, and steel value of launches the enemy forced you to make. Unit value is the template's CFG steel cost, read from the same CFG the production panel quotes, never a second price list. A drone killed by an interceptor counts once, as a destroyed unit for its owner and as a forced launch for the defender, and both entries are recorded because both are true; the readout defines the net so nothing double counts inside the net itself. Shared readouts exported in the readout family pattern (per nation destroyed, lost, forced, suffered, and net). No rule reads the ledger: no price, odds estimate, AI decision, research choice, or win check may consult it in this cycle; it is a scoreboard, not a currency, and the win and lose conditions are unchanged. The EW arms race, through the existing research path: exactly two new research items, bought with the same researchPoints pool and the same start of day decision shape as Drone Gen 2, for both nations at identical costs. (a) Drone Gen 3, requiring Drone Gen 2, raising the nation's drone generation from 2 to 3 (a nation that has not researched Gen 2 is generation 1; Gen 2 makes it 2); whether Gen 3 also changes the drone wing's printed attack and defense is loop tuning, stated in the log; the generation number itself is the counter that matters. (b) Jamming Gen 1, then Jamming Gen 2, in order, raising the nation's jamming generation from 0. The counter rule is one formula in one shared readout: a drone wing's effectiveness percent in a battle is 100 plus a loop tuned step (the prescribed shape is 25) times (its nation's drone generation minus the opposing nation's jamming generation), clamped to a stated floor and cap (the prescribed shape is 50 to 150). The readout multiplies the drone wing's attack and defense inside unitStats, so stackPower, resolveBattle, the preview, and the AI's shared estimate all see the same number by construction, and no other unit type is touched by it. Interceptors are not modified by jamming in this cycle (a stated limit, not an oversight: the generation counter governs drone fighting power; whether jamming should also blunt launches is parked below). AI parity: the Dominion lives under every part of this identically; it launches from the same stock under the same rule when the player attacks with drones, its launches and losses enter its ledger by the same code, it buys interceptors through the same priced path, and it makes its research choices (Gen 3, jamming) through the existing start of day aiResearch decision on start of day numbers, with any pacing or preference rule stated in the log as a spending rule, never a discount or a private price; its drone effectiveness is computed by the same readout against the player's jamming generation. Exit criteria: node check clean on every JS file, dash byte scan zero, existing suite green except where a test legitimately pins pre EW drone battle behavior (any such change named in the log with its reason), and builder spot checks showing: a staged attack with drones against a stocked defender launches exactly the stated number of interceptors, costs the defender the stated steel in the ledger, and kills the drones by the interceptor rule; the same attack with infantry only launches none; the same attack against an empty stock launches none; the effectiveness readout returns the exact stated percent at generation differences of minus 1, 0, and plus 1; and AI parity in isolation (identical staged battle with nations swapped gives mirrored ledger and launch numbers).
- Step 2, UI: the scoreboard and the EW state, legible at the moment of use. A scoreboard surface in the existing panel structure: both nations' exchange figures from the readouts, destroyed, lost, launches forced and suffered with their steel values, and the net exchange line in plain words that states who is bleeding faster and by how much. The figures update every render from the readouts only. The attack preview gains the drone lines in the meeting battle pattern: if the selected stack contains drone wings and the defender holds interceptor stock, the preview states how many launches the attack would trigger, what they cost the defender, and that the targeted drones die to them, plus the drone effectiveness percent for the battle with the two generation numbers that produced it (your drone generation against their jamming generation, and the reverse where relevant); a preview that hides either number fails this step. Research surfaces: the research area shows Drone Gen 3 and both jamming generations with their point costs, prerequisites, and current state, in the Drone Gen 2 button pattern; the unit card for a drone wing states its nation's current drone generation; the enemy card shows the Dominion's drone generation, jamming generation, and interceptor stock by the same readouts, so the arms race reads as a shared race, not a player menu. Exit criteria: a new browser check in the established pattern (tools/drone-ew-check.js or an extension of an existing check, the loop's choice, recorded) asserting the scoreboard's figures after a staged exchange, the preview's launch and effectiveness lines, and the enemy card's generation and stock numbers, with every expectation computed from the sim readouts and CFG, not hardcoded; all prior browser checks still pass at their recorded totals (manpower 15, lore 116, efficiency 15, fort 17, browser 6, unless a check is legitimately extended and its new total recorded); no horizontal scroll at 390 px; suite green; byte identity to tools/baseline-cycle11.txt is not required of this step if it touches no sim code, and if it does, the step stops and the change belongs to step 1 or 3.
- Step 3, tests and balance: pin the exchange, prove it moves in real campaigns. Formal tests in the established patterns pinning: launches (one per attacking drone wing up to stock, none for infantry only attacks, none from an empty stock, the drone removed by the interceptor rule and counted exactly once in the ledger); cost asymmetry (one forced launch's CFG cost exceeds one drone wing's full CFG cost, by the margin step 1 recorded); ledger exactness (a staged battle's destroyed, lost, forced, and suffered figures equal hand summed CFG costs, the net equals its definition, and two identical staged battles give identical ledgers); the generation counter (the effectiveness readout at generation differences minus 1, 0, plus 1, its clamp at the floor and cap, and a battle fought through the readout dealing the readout's numbers, with jamming affecting drone wings only, never infantry); research gating (Gen 3 refused without Gen 2, Jamming Gen 2 refused without Gen 1, points deducted exactly, identical costs for both nations); and AI parity through the real tick path (the Cycle 9 and 11 pattern). One non vacuity mutant shown failing exactly its target test, counts recorded, and verified clean against the pre step suite (the Cycle 11 mutant discipline); the judge suggests, and the loop may substitute a sharper one: interceptor launches free for the enemy (not entered in its suffered ledger), failing exactly the parity or ledger test. The mechanic must be proven to move in real play, not only in staged tests, in the binding trace pattern: at least one recorded trace on a standard seed through public commands only, in which real campaign battles trigger launches and the scoreboard's net moves off zero, with the trace's numbers reported; if the harness profiles produce no launches, that is reported honestly with the reason traced, a scripted drone forward profile through public commands supplies the trace, and no tuning slice is made to force the harness profiles to bind; if a profile does produce launches, the per profile exchange figures are reported beside the trace. Balance: the full rerun on the 8 standard seeds against Jash's ruling, which is the exit bar, not byte identity (EW is a real combat mechanic, so numbers will move; movement is reported per seed and per profile against tools/baseline-cycle11.txt): passive capital falls on day 30 to 45 on all 8 seeds; sensible wins 8 of 8 through the public command path with at least 20 percent of starting strength left, reported both with reinforcements counted and counting only surviving starting units; reckless loses 8 of 8. Any broken band is fixed by one small tuning slice at a time (one CFG number or one pacing rule per commit), never a one shot rebalance, and wins must come from intended mechanics, never from a defect. A new committed baseline, tools/baseline-cycle12.txt, in the harness's own format. BACKLOG.md and DECISIONS_FOR_JASH.md updated with no contradictions, including an honest statement of what the scoreboard does not do (it decides nothing, pays for nothing, and changes no win condition).
- Step 4, judge: a fresh judge with no builder context, grading against the bible and this prescription, independently rerunning the suite, the balance rerun against the ruling bands and tools/baseline-cycle12.txt, and all browser checks including the new EW check; verifying in code that every exchange and effectiveness number traces to the CFG costs and the one shared readout, that the ledger is read by no rule, price, odds estimate, or AI decision, and that the AI launches, researches, and bleeds under the identical rules; and reproducing the step 3 movement trace and the non vacuity mutant. A pass requires the exchange demonstrably moving in real play, parity proven, and every ruling band met.
- Taste parked for Jash by the judge, not decided by the prescription: whether interceptor launches should stay automatic, or become a player choice (launch or hold stock) once the scoreboard has taught the exchange (automatic is this cycle's loop default for legibility, not a ruling); the interceptor's flavor, its name and whether it reads as a missile, a counter drone, or a crewed interceptor wing (the loop uses the plain word interceptor until Jash rules); whether the scoreboard should stay steel only, or a later cycle should price losses in a combined steel and manpower figure (steel only is this cycle's shape, because steel is the currency every asset already carries); whether jamming should, in a later cycle, also reduce interceptor launches or their accuracy (this cycle deliberately keeps jamming on drone fighting power only); and whether Drone Gen 3 should change how a drone wing looks on the map beyond its numbers (the Civ visible progression debt, recorded since Cycle 5, is Jash's call when he sees the generations on screen).

This run advanced exactly one step: step 1 only, the simulation. Step 2 (scoreboard and EW state on screen), step 3 (formal tests, the real campaign trace, and the ruling balance), and step 4 (judge) remain. ### Sync in
- With PYTHONPATH set to /opt/muse/skills/custom-connector-setup/bin and /tmp/ashes-gh-sync removed first, master fetched cleanly and diffed identical to local HEAD 9373121, file for file. Nothing copied in, nothing overwritten.
