### Tuning chosen by the loop (recorded per the prescription)
- Interceptor: CFG.interceptorStart 4 per nation. The priced production path is a third production template, interceptor, in CFG.unitTypes: 50 steel over 5 build days (10 steel per day) and 10 manpower paid at queue time through queueProduction. One interceptor's steel cost, 50, is 3.33 times one drone wing's steel cost, 15 (and its full listed price, 50 steel plus 10 manpower, exceeds the drone wing's 15 steel plus 25 manpower on the steel side by the wide margin the prescription requires; the arithmetic is stated here so step 3 can pin it). A finished Interceptor adds 1 to the nation's interceptor stockpile and deploys no map unit; the template's attack, defense, and strength are never used in a battle.
- The launch rule, stated and pinned by the spot checks below: inside fightRounds, the shared combat path that resolveBattle and every movementPhase engagement call, when side B fights in defense mode against a side A of another nation, side B's nation launches one interceptor per attacking drone wing, up to its stock on hand, before the first round. Targets are the attacking drone wings in unit id order. A launched interceptor consumes 1 stock, is valued at 50 steel in the ledger, and destroys its target outright: the drone dies to the interceptor, not to battle damage, its attack never counts in any round, and it is recorded once as a destroyed unit for the defender and a lost unit for its owner, never again as a battle death. Meeting battles, where both sides fight in attack mode, launch nothing; a defender with zero stock launches nothing and the battle proceeds exactly as before. The same rule binds both nations by construction, because there is one code path.
- The exchange ledger: state.exchange per nation, { destroyed, lost, forced, suffered } in steel, accrued at the moment each fact happens inside fightRounds. Unit value is the template's CFG steelCost (infantry 30, drone 15), read from the same CFG the production panel quotes. Battle deaths are priced from the strengths the rounds start with, after any launches, so an interceptor kill is never counted twice. The net readout is destroyed plus forced minus lost minus suffered, so the staged drone that dies forcing a 50 steel launch nets its owner plus 35 on that fact alone (15 lost against 50 forced, before the battle around it). No rule reads the ledger: no price, odds estimate, AI decision, research choice, or win check consults it, verified in code and by a spot check that stuffing the ledger changes no unit stat.
- The EW counter: CFG.ewStepPct 25, CFG.ewFloorPct 50, CFG.ewCapPct 150, in the one shared readout droneEffectiveness(state, nationId, opposingId): 100 plus 25 times (the nation's drone generation minus the opposing nation's jamming generation), clamped to 50 to 150. Drone generation is 1 at the start, 2 with Drone Gen 2, 3 with Drone Gen 3. One honest consequence of the prescribed formula, recorded rather than smoothed: at the start the difference is plus 1 for both nations (generation 1 against jamming 0), so starting drone wings fight at 125 percent, and the floor of 50 can never bind with the shipped generation ranges (the difference runs from minus 1 to plus 3, so the lowest reachable value is 75 and the cap binds from a difference of plus 3, where 175 clamps to 150). unitStats multiplies a drone wing's attack and defense by the readout, after the generation base stats and before supply and walls, so stackPower, resolveBattle, the preview, and the AI estimate all see the same number; no other unit type is touched. Jamming modifies drone fighting power only and never blunts a launch, the stated limit the prescription prescribed.
- Research: Drone Gen 3 costs CFG.droneGen3Cost 90 points, requires Drone Gen 2, and raises the drone base stats to attack 6, defense 4 (CFG.droneGen3), a loop tuning choice stated here per the prescription. Jamming Gen 1 then Gen 2, in order through the one researchJamming function, cost CFG.jammingCosts 50 then 80 points. All three are bought from the same researchPoints pool at identical costs for both nations.
- AI rules, both stated as spending rules at identical prices, never discounts: aiResearch buys one item per tick on start of day numbers in a save priority (Drone Gen 2, then Jamming Gen 1, then Drone Gen 3, then Jamming Gen 2; while an earlier item is unowned it saves for it and buys nothing later). The Dominion replenishes interceptors through the same production path: when its stock is at 1 or none and its line 2 stands idle, it retooles line 2 to Interceptors and queues one; once the stock is back above 1 and line 2 stands idle on the Interceptor template, it retooles back to Drone Wings. The player has no such auto rule; retooling a line to Interceptors is the player's own choice, with its UI surface in step 2.

### What was built
- js/sim.js only, plus three named test repins below. New CFG: droneGen3Cost, jammingCosts, ewStepPct, ewFloorPct, ewCapPct, interceptorStart, droneGen3 base stats, and the interceptor unit template. New readouts, all exported: droneGeneration, jammingGeneration, droneEffectiveness, interceptorStock, interceptorCost, exchangeRecord, exchangeDestroyed, exchangeLost, exchangeForced, exchangeSuffered, exchangeNet. New research functions, exported: researchDroneGen3, researchJamming. createGame gives both nations droneGen3 false, jammingGen 0, interceptors at the CFG start, and a zeroed exchange ledger. productionPhase completes an Interceptor into the stockpile with its own log line. fightRounds carries the launch rule, the ledger writes for launches and battle deaths, and a launch log line naming the count and the steel. aiResearch and the aiTakeTurn production block carry the AI rules above.
- A bug found and fixed inside this step, before any commit: the first aiResearch draft bought whatever it could afford in order, so at 50 points it bought Jamming Gen 1 on the way to Drone Gen 2 at 60, spent the pool, and the Dominion never fielded Gen 2 in a full campaign (measured: jammingGen 1, 55 points, no Gen 2 beat on seeds 42 and 31337). The save priority above is the fix, and the research clock and beats tests pass on it (Gen 2 beat by the enemy on day 21, as before).

The ledger is read by no rule: every exchange reference in js/sim.js is the header comment, ensureExchange, the recordExchange write path inside fightRounds, the readout family, the createGame initializer, and the exports, with no occurrence in any price, odds, AI decision, research function, or win check; in js/main.js the only readers are renderExchange display reads, and the scoreboard's own on screen explain states that it decides nothing. Jamming never blunts a launch: fightRounds contains no jamming reference, the launch count depends only on attacking drone wings and stock, and the UI jamming explain prints that limit, asserted in the drone-ew check.

### Cycle 13 prescription from the judge, accepted and logged here
Cycle 13 is Intel and Fog, next in the deferred order the Cycle 8 judge set (after Cycle 13: navy). No carried flag exists, so Cycle 13 has no step 0; it starts at step 1. The judge's verified statement of the current state: there is no intel, fog, recon, spy, agent, sight, or visibility mechanic anywhere in js/sim.js, js/main.js, or index.html. The map renders every province, unit, factory, and fortification in full for both nations; the attack preview gives the exact shared stackPower numbers for any defended neighbor at any time; the enemy card gives the Dominion's exact pool, intake, factory levels, open lines, fortified provinces, generations, interceptor stock, and exchange record for free. Drone wings, the bible's recon arm, are purely combat units and interceptor targets today: they see no further than infantry. Intel as sight does not exist yet in any form. The bible's framing, which is the law for this cycle: intel as sight; the spy network is drone recon plus agents; it lifts fog and finds soft spots; spying is how you see, not a side menu. Fog of war and recon must be legible on screen, explain themselves at the moment of use, and must not create Stellaris style opacity: every hidden thing must say what would reveal it, in plain words, where the player is looking at it. Theater scale and v1 scoped per the bible's out list: no world map, no diplomacy system, no agent characters or agent management screen, no counterintelligence game. The cycle's one visible number: for each province, its intel freshness, the day it was last seen live, with today for a province under live observation and never for one never seen; the headline surface number is provinces under live observation now (a count of the 70), shown where the player plans. The one shared readout: intelState for a nation and a province, returning live, remembered, or dark, computed identically for both nations from the same sight sources, and read by the map, the inspector, the preview, and the surfaces below, and no other rule.
- Step 1, sim: fog state, sight sources, snapshots, and the agent path. Fog is an information layer only in this cycle: it changes no combat, supply, production, price, odds, research, movement, or win rule, and no battle number; stackPower and every other shared estimate keep computing true numbers in the sim, and what fog gates is what the UI may show (step 2) and what the recorded snapshot holds; this limit is stated in the log and in BACKLOG.md, in the exchange ledger's honest limit pattern. Sight sources, one CFG number per parameter, identical for both nations: a province a nation owns is live, and so is every province adjacent to an owned province; every province holding a unit of the nation is live, and so is every province adjacent to one of its units; a drone wing extends sight one province further (sight range 2 from a drone wing's province, through the province graph, regardless of the owner of the ground passed over, because it flies), which is what makes drone recon a distinct verb from infantry presence and ties this cycle to Cycle 12's drone arm; an agent (below) makes its province live. intelState is computed from these sources by one exported readout family (intelState, lastSeenDay, isLive or equivalent shapes), with no second computation anywhere. Snapshots: at the end of each tick, in a stated phase in the tick order, each nation records a snapshot for every province live to it that day: the day, the owner, the fortification level and any fort work in progress, the factory level, rail presence where relevant, and the units present with their nation, type, count, and total strength. A remembered province shows its snapshot and its day; a dark province has no snapshot. Snapshots are recorded in state in the beats and textures pattern (a per nation, per province record), deterministically, and no rule reads a snapshot except the display readouts of step 2: no price, odds estimate, AI decision, research choice, or win check may consult intel state or snapshots in this cycle, verified by grep in step 4. The scripted AI's decisions are unchanged by fog in this cycle and it does not read intel; that is a stated scope limit for the AI, recorded in BACKLOG.md, not a hidden asymmetry, because the sight computation itself is identical for both nations and the AI parity pins below cover the computation and the snapshots. Agents, the second half of the bible's spy network, in the smallest v1 shape: an agent is built only through a priced production path in the Interceptor pattern (a production template whose completion adds to an agent stockpile instead of deploying a map unit, at a loop tuned steel cost over build days plus a manpower cost at queue time through the shared queueProduction path, all identical for both nations), and is placed only through one public command, plantAgent or its equivalent, which spends one agent from stock to make one chosen enemy or neutral province (any province the nation does not own) live to that nation from the next intel phase until the province changes owner or the campaign ends. One agent per province per nation; a second placement on the same province is refused with a numbered, legible reason; placement on a province the nation owns is refused the same way. An agent reveals its province only, not its neighbors (the drone is the wide eye, the agent is the deep one). Whether agents should ever be removable, killable, or reveal neighbors is parked below, not built. The Dominion builds and places agents through the identical priced paths at identical prices, under one stated spending rule in the aiTakeTurn pattern (for example, it plants on the player's capital row staging province when it holds an agent and that province is not already live to it; the exact target rule is loop tuning, stated in the log, never a discount or a free placement). Exit criteria: node --check clean on every JS file, dash byte scan zero, existing suite green except where a test legitimately pins full information behavior (any such change named in the log with its reason; the expectation is none, because this step touches no displayed text and no rule), and builder spot checks showing: at game start each nation sees its own ground and its border live and the enemy heartland dark, with mirrored counts; moving a drone wing to the front makes a province two hops away live that infantry at the same province cannot see; a snapshot records on the day a province is live and does not update on days it is not; an agent built through the priced path and placed through the public command makes its target live and its snapshot record, and a refused placement charges nothing.
- Step 2, UI: fog on the map, legible at the moment of use. The map renders three visibly distinct states for provinces not owned by the player: live (normal rendering), remembered (dimmed or hatched in the supply overlay's visual language, with unit chips replaced by the snapshot's ghost figures marked with their day, or province military detail suppressed if ghost chips are not built; whichever shape is chosen is stated in the log and the other is not claimed), and dark (a stated fog treatment under which geography, province name, and terrain remain, because the theater map is known, but owner color beyond the last snapshot, units, factories, forts, and rail state are not shown). Owned and live player provinces render exactly as today. A legend on or beside the map states the three states and the sight rules in plain words (your provinces and their neighbors, your units and their neighbors, drone wings see one province further, an agent watches its province), so the system explains itself where it is seen. The province inspector is the moment of use surface: for a live enemy province it shows the true current detail it shows today; for a remembered province it shows the snapshot with its day stated in its first line (for example, last seen on day 18, this may have changed) and nothing current presented as current; for a dark province it states plainly that nothing is known beyond the map, what would reveal it (bring a unit next to it, bring a drone wing within two provinces, or plant an agent there), and shows no military figures at all. Soft spots, the bible's payoff, surfaced where a decision is made: the attack preview for a defended neighbor keeps its exact shared numbers only when the target province is live to the player; when the target is remembered, the preview shows the snapshot's defenders, fort level, and day, labels them as last seen, and states that the true numbers are not known today and how to make them known; when dark, it shows no enemy figures and states the same in plain words. The player may still order any attack legal today: fog gates information, never orders, in this cycle. The scoreboard, exchange, research, manpower, and nation aggregate surfaces from earlier cycles stay as they are (they are war level aggregates, not province intel); whether they should ever be fogged is parked below, and BACKLOG.md states this limit openly. The agent surface: the production panel reaches the agent template by retool like the Interceptor path, the nation card or intel surface shows agent stock, and planting is done by selecting an eligible non owned province and using a stated Plant agent control in the province card, with refusals surfacing their sim reason in the panel notice pattern from Cycle 11. The intel headline (provinces under live observation now, of 70) sits on the nation card or the map legend from the shared readout only. Exit criteria: a new browser check in the established pattern (tools/intel-check.js) asserting, with expectations computed from the sim readouts and CFG and never hardcoded: the three map states on a fresh game, the inspector's live, remembered, and dark wordings with their snapshot day and reveal instructions, the preview's exact numbers on a live target and their absence with the plain reason on a remembered and a dark target, the agent stock and a placement through the real control making its province live on the map, and no horizontal scroll at 390 px. All prior browser checks still pass at their recorded totals (drone-ew 28, lore 116, manpower 15, efficiency 15, fort 17, browser 6), unless a check legitimately asserts a now fogged figure and is extended or adjusted with the change named in the log and its new total recorded; suite green; if this step needs a sim change, the step stops and the change belongs to step 1 or 3.
- Step 3, tests and balance: pin sight, prove recon moves the picture in real campaigns. Formal tests in the established patterns pinning: the sight computation (owned ground and its neighbors live, a unit's province and its neighbors live, a drone wing's second ring live where infantry at the same province sees dark, mirrored identically for the Dominion); snapshots (recorded with the true figures on a live day, frozen while the province is not live even as the true figures change underneath, updated on the next live day, freshness day equal to the snapshot day); the agent path (built only through the priced production path at the stated steel, days, and manpower for both nations, placement spending exactly one stock, refusal cases charging and placing nothing, the placed province live and recording snapshots); information only (a full campaign with intel recording on and off, if a CFG gate is built for the tests, identical in every field except the intel records, in the textures zero effect pattern; if no gate is built, the equivalent pin is that no staged battle, price, or AI outcome differs between two games that differ only in agent placement); and AI parity through the real tick path (the Cycle 9 and 11 pattern: identical staged positions give both nations identical intel states and snapshots with nations swapped, and the Dominion's agent spending rule fires through the shared paths at the shared prices). One non vacuity mutant shown failing exactly its target test, counts recorded, and verified clean against the pre step suite (the Cycle 11 and 12 mutant discipline); the judge suggests, and the loop may substitute a sharper one: drone wings sight range computed as 1 instead of 2 (drones see no further than infantry), failing exactly the drone recon pin. The mechanic must be proven to move in real play, in the binding trace pattern: at least one recorded trace on a standard seed through public commands only, in which bringing a drone wing forward lifts fog on a named enemy province that infantry alone could not see and reveals a soft spot fact the player could act on (a fort level, an absent or weak garrison, or a snapshot that changes an attack decision the trace names), with the before and after intel state and the snapshot figures reported; if the harness profiles never place a drone where its second ring matters, that is reported honestly with the reason traced, a scripted recon forward profile through public commands supplies the trace, and no tuning slice is made to force the harness profiles to bind. Balance: the full rerun on the 8 standard seeds against Jash's ruling, which is the exit bar: passive capital falls on day 30 to 45 on all 8 seeds; sensible wins 8 of 8 through the public command path with at least 20 percent of starting strength left, reported both with reinforcements counted and counting only surviving starting units; reckless loses 8 of 8. Because fog changes no rule in this prescription, the expected result is a rerun byte identical to tools/baseline-cycle12.txt except for any intel fields the harness report legitimately gains (in the Cycle 12 step 3 exchange fields pattern, added only if a trace claim needs them); any other moved field is a mechanical effect and a step failure until removed or explained as a named, prescribed change. A new committed baseline, tools/baseline-cycle13.txt, in the harness's own format if the report shape changes, otherwise a recorded byte identity to the Cycle 12 baseline and no new file claimed. BACKLOG.md and DECISIONS_FOR_JASH.md updated with no contradictions, including the honest limits (fog gates information, not orders or battle outcomes; the scripted AI does not read intel; the aggregate panels are not fogged).
- Step 4, judge: a fresh judge with no builder context, grading against the bible and this prescription, independently rerunning the suite, the balance rerun against the ruling bands and the Cycle 13 baseline state, and all browser checks including the new intel check; verifying in code that every intel figure traces to the one shared sight readout and snapshot record, that no rule, price, odds estimate, AI decision, research choice, or win check reads intel state or snapshots, that launches, exchange, and every earlier system are untouched in behavior, and that the AI builds and plants agents under the identical priced rules; and reproducing the step 3 recon trace and the non vacuity mutant. A pass requires fog demonstrably lifting in real play through drone recon or an agent, parity of the sight computation proven, every ruling band met, and no surface presenting remembered or dark information as current fact.
- Taste parked for Jash by the judge, not decided by the prescription: whether dark provinces should hide even geography, names, and owner color (this cycle's loop default keeps the theater map known and hides only military fact, for legibility); whether remembered provinces should show ghost unit chips on the map or snapshot numbers only in the inspector; whether the war level aggregate panels (enemy pool, generations, stock, fortified province list) should be fogged in a later cycle or stay known as general war intelligence; whether the scripted AI should become fog bound in a later cycle, attacking only what it can see, with the balance risk that carries; whether agents should be removable or counterable, gain neighbors, or get a flavor name and service beyond the plain word agent; and whether a later cycle should add a non combat recon sortie order for drone wings (holding position to watch), beyond this cycle's passive sight from wherever a wing stands.

### Tuning and rules chosen by the loop (recorded per the prescription)
- Sight sources, one CFG number each, identical for both nations: CFG.ownedSightRange 1 (owned ground plus one province past it), CFG.unitSightRange 1 (a unit's province plus one past it), CFG.droneSightRange 2 (a drone wing's province plus two past it, through the province graph regardless of the owner of the ground passed over, because it flies). A planted agent makes its province live, that province only, never its neighbors (the drone is the wide eye, the agent is the deep one, in the prescription's own framing).
- Agent pricing, in the Interceptor pattern: a fourth production template, agent, in CFG.unitTypes at 40 steel over 4 build days (10 steel per day, kept whole) and 60 manpower paid in full at queue time through queueProduction, between a drone wing's 25 crew and an infantry division's 120. A finished Agent adds 1 to the nation's agent stockpile (nation.agents, starting at 0, so the priced path is the only source) and deploys no map unit; its attack, defense, and strength are never used in a battle.
- plantAgent, the one public placement command: it spends exactly 1 stock to watch one province the nation does not own, from placement until that province changes owner or the campaign ends; one agent per province per nation. Refusals are legible and charge and plant nothing: planting on a province the nation owns, planting a second agent on a province already watched, and planting with an empty stock (whose reason names the build price from CFG: 40 steel over 4 days plus 60 manpower). An agent whose province has changed hands counts for nothing everywhere, whether or not intelPhase has cleared the record, and intelPhase clears such records at the end of the tick.
- Snapshots: intelPhase runs in the tick after the dead are removed and before beatPhase, gated by CFG.campaignIntel in the beats and textures pattern. For each nation it records state.intel[nation].snapshots[province] for every province live to that nation that day: { day, owner, fortLevel, fortBuild (a copy of the work in progress or null), factoryLevel, rail (true if any edge touching the province carries rail), units (the units present grouped by nation and type, sorted, with count and total strength) }. A province not live keeps its last snapshot untouched. The readout family is the only sight computation: intelState (live, remembered, or dark), intelIsLive, intelLastSeenDay (today while live, the snapshot day while remembered, null while dark), intelSnapshot, intelLiveProvinces, and intelLiveCount. Fog gates information only in this cycle: no combat, supply, production, price, odds, research, movement, or win rule reads intel state or a snapshot, and the win and lose conditions are unchanged. The headline surface number for step 2 is intelLiveCount (provinces under live observation now, of 70).
- The Dominion's agent spending rules, stated, at the identical prices through the identical paths, never a discount or a free placement: placement, when it holds an agent in stock it plants it on the player's capital whenever that province is not its own and carries no agent of its own yet (an agent there watches durably, so the rule consults only its own stock and its own planted agents, never fog); building, it builds at most one agent, only while it holds none in stock, has none planted, and has no line on the Agent template already, and only on a line standing idle while its field army and queue reach the same 14 unit cap its general queueing works to, so the order displaces no combat order, and only when its manpower pool pays the shared 60 in full. Two guards keep the rules from converting its army pipeline into an agent pipeline: the build guard above, and a restore rule that returns an idle Agent template line to Drone Wings once an agent is planted or in stock, so the general queueing never orders agents by accident. The scripted AI is not fog bound in this cycle and reads no intel state and no snapshot for any decision, the prescription's stated scope limit, recorded in BACKLOG.md.

### Lessons
- An on and off comparison is only as honest as its strip: the first draft of the information only test both overclaimed (a fully empty intel record with recording off, which the planted agent record contradicts by design) and, in its first repair attempt, understripped toward a fudge (deleting agent stock fields from the comparison on a speculative theory). The measured fact was cleaner than either draft: strip state.intel and nothing else, and the whole campaigns match, log included. Verify the diff field by field before writing the assertion, and let the test state the one gating precision (what campaignIntel does and does not gate) in its own comment.
- A mirrored record comparison must normalize the label that mirrors: two snapshot unit lists from opposite nations can never be deep equal, because each record names its own nation. Comparing the mirrored shape (type, count, strength) and saying so in the assertion keeps the parity claim exact without pretending the labels match.

### Judge fix-now Flag 1, carried to Cycle 14 step 0 (the judge's prescription)
- The defect: in renderProvinceCard (js/main.js), the factory button is set unconditionally from the true province after the intel branches: its cost is CFG.factoryCostPerLevel (40) times (factoryLevel plus 1), its label reads "Build / Upgrade Factory (N eq)", and at max level it reads "Factory at max level". No intel state is consulted. For a remembered province it therefore shows the current level, not the snapshot level its inspector just labelled last seen; for a dark province it shows a current military economic fact the dark inspector body explicitly says is not shown. The exact current factory level is recoverable from the label (level equals N divided by 40, minus 1, with the max level text a third distinguishable state).
- Evidence from the judge's own browser probe (unmodified game, seed 42, no staging, 0 page errors): dark Khessograd (p9_3, true factory level 2, dark in the node mirror) renders "Build / Upgrade Factory (120 eq)"; dark Ostmarsh (p8_3, true factory level 0) renders "Build / Upgrade Factory (40 eq)". Clicking any dark province in ordinary play shows it. tools/intel-check.js passes 29 of 29 because it asserts the dark tile, the inspector body, and the preview, but never this button; the fort button beside it is safe (a constant text for non owned provinces), which is the in codebase precedent for the fix shape. The remembered half is verified by the code path (one unconditional computation serving every selected province); the judge did not stage a separate remembered browser probe for the button and said so.
- Why it blocks a clean PASS, in the judge's framing: the step 2 prescription requires the dark surface to show no military figures at all, and the step 4 pass bar requires no surface presenting remembered or dark information as current fact.
- Prescribed fix, Cycle 14 step 0: in renderProvinceCard, when the selected province's intel state is not live, the factory button label must be a constant carrying no level derived number (the fort button's constant label pattern). Behavior for owned provinces (always live) and for live enemy provinces is unchanged. Extend tools/intel-check.js with assertions, expectations computed from a node mirror and CFG as the check already does elsewhere: the factory button text is identical for two dark provinces whose true factory levels differ, and a remembered province's factory button shows the same constant rather than its current or snapshot level cost. ### Cycle 14 prescription from the judge, accepted and logged here
Cycle 14 is Navy, last in the deferred order the Cycle 8 judge set. The bible's scope is the law: navy at theater scale means coastal control, river crossings, and a blockade pressure on the economy. The bible's out list binds: no naval invasions, no world map, no sea provinces beyond theater scope, no diplomacy. Flotillas never carry units and no unit ever enters a water tile; crossings remain land moves across the map's existing typed river edges, and coastal control is fought over the existing coastal flagged provinces. The cycle's one visible number: blockade pressure, the steel income a nation is losing to blockade today, shown where the player plans, computed by one shared readout. Carried flag: Flag 1 above is Cycle 14 step 0.
- Step 0, fix the carried flag (factory button fog leak): as prescribed under Flag 1 above. Exit criteria: the constant label in place for non live provinces; tools/intel-check.js extended with the two dark province comparison and the remembered assertion, run standalone, its new total recorded in the log; suite 98 green; balance rerun byte identical to tools/baseline-cycle13.txt; all other browser checks at their recorded totals (drone-ew 28, lore 116, manpower 15, efficiency 15, fort 17, browser 6). Observation 2's preview line presence gating may be closed in this step at the loop's discretion and is recorded either way, but it is not an exit criterion.
- Step 1, sim: flotillas, coastal control, river crossings, blockade. One CFG number per parameter, identical for both nations. (a) A fifth production template, flotilla, in the Interceptor and Agent pattern: priced in steel over build days plus manpower at queue time through the shared queueProduction path, completing into a flotilla stockpile and deploying no map unit. (b) One public placement command, deployFlotilla or its equivalent: spends one stock to station a flotilla at one owned coastal or river province, one per province per nation, with legible numbered refusals (not owned, not coastal or river, already stationed, empty stock) that charge and place nothing; a stationed flotilla is removed when its province changes owner, in the agent expiry pattern. (c) Coastal control, one shared readout family (coastalControl or equivalent): a coastal province is controlled by the nation that owns it and stations a flotilla there or holds it with units, in a stated precedence the log records; the theater count of controlled coastal provinces per nation is the headline input. (d) Blockade: while a nation controls at least a loop tuned share (a CFG count or fraction) of the enemy's home coastal provinces, the enemy's daily steel income is reduced by CFG.blockadeSteelPct through incomePhase and no other path, computed from the one readout; the readout reports today's blockade loss per nation in steel, and no price, odds, AI decision, or win check other than the stated income effect reads it. (e) River crossings: attacking across a river typed edge applies one named modifier, CFG.riverCrossingPct, to the attacking stack's attack inside the shared stackPower and unitStats path, so battle, preview, and AI estimate all see the same number; a flotilla stationed at either endpoint province of that edge removes the penalty for its nation's crossings of that edge (the ferry and fire support rule, stated in the log). The Dominion builds, stations, blockades, and crosses under the identical priced paths and rules, under stated spending rules in the aiTakeTurn pattern (for example, it stations on its capital's coastal province first, then its river Spine province), and it reads no new private information. Exit criteria: node --check clean on every JS file, dash byte scan zero, existing suite green, and builder spot checks showing: a flotilla built only through the priced path for both nations; each deploy refusal charging nothing; coastal counts mirrored on identical starting ground; blockade switching the enemy steel income by exactly the readout amount on the day the threshold is met and by zero the day it is not; a river crossing battle costing the attacker exactly the named percent through stackPower, and the penalty gone with a flotilla at either bank; a province changing owner clearing its flotilla.
- Step 2, UI: navy on screen, legible at the moment of use. The map marks coastal provinces and stationed flotillas with a badge in the existing badge language, and a river edge under flotilla support is distinguishable from one that is not. The nation card carries the blockade lines from the readout only (your coastal control count, the enemy's, your steel lost to blockade today and the enemy's, each with the threshold stated in plain words). The province card gains the Deploy flotilla control in the Plant agent pattern (enabled on an eligible owned province, refusals surfacing their sim reason in the card notice, its reason on the button when the province class is ineligible), states a selected province's coastal and river status and any stationed flotilla, and states for a river province whether your crossings there are supported. The attack preview names the river crossing penalty inside the attack numbers for a river edge target, and states when a flotilla removes it, in the fortification preview pattern. The production panel reaches the flotilla template by retool (the panel already derives its retool list from CFG.unitTypes, so this is verified, not rebuilt). A short explain on the nation card or map legend states the whole system in plain words: flotillas are built, stationed, control coast, press blockade past the threshold, and support river crossings; they never carry troops and there are no invasions. Exit criteria: a new browser check in the established pattern (tools/navy-check.js) asserting, with expectations computed from the sim readouts and CFG and never hardcoded: the coastal and flotilla map marks, the blockade lines against the readout on a fresh game and on a staged blockaded game, the preview's crossing penalty line with and without a supporting flotilla, a deployment through the real control stationing a flotilla and moving the control count, a refusal surfacing in the notice, and no horizontal scroll at 390 px. All prior browser checks still pass at their recorded totals (intel at its step 0 total, drone-ew 28, lore 116, manpower 15, efficiency 15, fort 17, browser 6), unless a check legitimately asserts a figure the navy surfaces change and is extended with the change named in the log; suite green; if this step needs a sim change, the step stops and the change belongs to step 1 or 3.

A pass requires blockade or a supported crossing demonstrably changing an outcome in real play, parity proven, every ruling band met, and no surface stating a navy figure the readout does not hold.

### Lessons
- A differential assertion is the strongest shape a gating check can take: two provinces differing only in the hidden fact must render identical text. It caught the defect exactly (2 failures, both new, with the leaked labels printed), it cannot pass on the pre fix code by accident, and it needs no hardcoded level, because the pair and both would be labels are computed from the mirror and CFG.
- A discretionary observation can conflict with a prescribed surface from an earlier cycle: Observation 2's suggested gating would have removed the dark preview line that Cycle 13 step 2 prescribed and pinned. When two prescriptions pull against each other, keep the required one, record the optional one as not closed with its reason in both the log and the backlog, and never let silence read as closure.

### Tuning chosen by the loop (recorded per the prescription)
- Flotilla template: CFG.unitTypes.flotilla, 40 steel over 4 build days (10 steel per day) and 30 manpower paid at queue time through queueProduction, in the Interceptor and Agent pattern. A finished Flotilla adds 1 to the nation's flotilla stockpile and deploys no map unit; its attack, defense, and strength are never used. Both nations start with 0 in stock, like agents.
- Coastal control precedence, stated: a coastal province is controlled by the nation that owns it and stations a flotilla there (flotilla precedence); failing that, by its owner holding it with units; an owned coastal province with neither is controlled by no one. On identical starting ground both nations therefore control 0 coastal provinces (each owns 10 coastal provinces, none garrisoned or stationed), mirrored exactly.
- Blockade: CFG.blockadeCoastalThreshold 3 (of the enemy's 10 home coastal provinces) and CFG.blockadeSteelPct 25. While a nation controls at least 3 of the opposing nation's home coastal provinces, the opposing nation loses 25 percent of its gross daily steel income, rounded down, subtracted in incomePhase and nowhere else. blockadeLoss is the readout: exactly the amount incomePhase subtracts on a threshold day, and 0 on any other day. No price, odds estimate, AI decision, research choice, or win check reads coastal control or the loss, verified by grep this step (the only readers are incomePhase, the readouts themselves, and the AI stationing rule's own province eligibility, which is placement of its own pieces, not a blockade read).
- River crossings: CFG.riverCrossingPct 25. Inside stackPower, when a target province is named in the context, each attacking unit loses 25 percent of its attack (rounded, floor 1) if the edge from its own province to the target is a river edge and no flotilla of its nation is stationed at either endpoint; a defense stack is never charged. Pricing per unit from its own province means a combined attack from two banks prices each column by the edge it actually crosses. fightRounds derives the target from the opposing side's province, so resolveBattle and every movementPhase engagement charge the crossing side automatically; road meetings charge both sides, each by its own edge, and province defenders in defense mode are never charged. The AI's attack estimate in aiTakeTurn now passes its target through the same context, so it decides with the penalized number.
- Dominion spending rules, stated, at identical prices: placement stations a held flotilla first on its river Spine province (provinceId(mapW/2, capital row), p5_3, which supports its capital row crossings), then its capital column coastal provinces, then any owned coastal province, then any owned river province, always through deployFlotilla. Building follows the agent pattern: only when its field army and queue reach the 14 unit cap, only while it holds fewer than 2 flotillas in stock and stationed together, only with no line already on the Flotilla template, and only at the full shared manpower price; an idle Flotilla template line at the 2 flotilla limit is restored to Drone Wings so general queueing never orders flotillas by accident.

When a mark must appear in a state another check defines by absence, name the new mark separately and say in the log which absence definition it respects.

### The tuning slice (commit 9354d29, one committed change: CFG.supplyMaxHops 8 to 10, plus the one BACKLOG sentence that quoted 8 hops)
- The known break going in: passive seed 2024 survives to day 151. Traced on the pre tuning code this run: the Dominion masses 7 units at p2_3 on day 30, supplied that day (supplyPenalty 0); from day 31 the stack's penalty grows 10 per day to the 50 cap and never falls, and the scripted AI's standing rule is that a group with any supply penalty does not attack at all, so the stack freezes two provinces from the capital while it attrits. The supply readout on day 35 names the mechanism exactly: p3_3 is supplied at exactly 8 hops, the old cap; p2_3, one rail edge west of p3_3, reads unsupplied, "line cut or too long", because it is 9 hops from the Dominion capital (the direct river edge p4_3 to p5_3 carries no rail, so the rail path detours through p5_2 and p4_2), and p1_3 beyond it is 10 hops. Before this cycle the same advance took the capital on day 36 in the brief window before the penalty accrued; the crossing delay on the unsupported flank rows (only the capital row crossing is flotilla supported) slowed it just enough for the cap to bind first.
- Candidates measured one at a time in scratch copies, in this order, and rejected on the record: (1) lowering CFG.riverCrossingPct: at 20, 15, 14, and 13 passive seed 2024 still survives; at 12 the band is restored, but at 12 the per unit rounding erases the penalty entirely for the standard units (an infantry attack of 4 becomes round(3.52) = 4, and a Gen 1 drone wing the same), leaving bite only on attack 5 and above, so the slice would restore the band by rounding the cycle's own prescribed mechanic away. (2) The AI stationing order extended to river provinces before coastal: no change on any seed (the Dominion stations exactly one flotilla in time, on p5_3, under either order). (3) The AI flotilla build gate lowered from the 14 unit cap to 10: no change on any seed. (4) The AI's out of supply attack rule: not changed; it is a stated bible brake (a group sitting out of supply does not attack at all), broader than this defect. ### Lessons
- The freeze's mechanism was one number past a cap, and the cap was the slice: the step 1 trace had the right stack and the right rule (out of supply groups never attack) but stopped one readout short. Reading computeSupply's own hops figure on the frozen province (p3_3 supplied at exactly the cap of 8, p2_3 at 9) turned a vague "supply freeze" into an exact distance, and the exact distance picked the slice. When a trace names a frozen state, quote the readout that measures the distance to the threshold, not only the rule that freezes.
- A tuning candidate can restore every band and still be the wrong slice, and the reason can be arithmetic, not taste: lowering the crossing percent to 12 passed all 32 rows, but per unit rounding at 12 erases the penalty for the two standard unit types, so the band would have been restored by quietly deleting the mechanic for most battles. Measure what a candidate does to the mechanic's own quoted numbers on standard units before accepting its balance table.
- A mechanic that binds nowhere in the standard profiles is a tally result, not a suspicion: instrumenting the harness profiles for one run (control counts and loss tracked daily) settled in minutes that blockade fires in 0 of 32 campaigns, which is what made the staged income trace the honest binding evidence instead of a claim that some profile must bind somewhere.

Direction: Jash's 2026-10-17 order for the free model loop, superseding the post Cycle 14 idle posture. The next cycles in order are Cycle 15 (campaign end screen with scoring), Cycle 16 (save and load, including save integrity and time step determinism tests), and Cycle 17 (playability pass). The 48 post Cycle 14 verification runs are closed history; they are not a reason to stay idle under the new order.

Step list for Cycle 15:
- Step 1: sim. One shared campaignScore readout and a campaignResult readout in js/sim.js only, computed from current state, with no rule reading them and no change to any win condition, price, odds, AI, or tick path.
- Step 2: UI. A campaign end screen that replaces the one line banner as the end surface, showing the result, the day, and the full scoring breakdown for both nations from the Step 1 readouts, with every component labelled in plain words and a New Game control. Legibility is law: the screen must state how each score number is earned.
- Step 3: tests and balance. Formal scoring tests (arithmetic at the stated weights, capital cases, determinism, zero mechanical effect, mirrored parity), a committed browser check for the end screen, and a balance rerun that must stay byte identical to tools/baseline-cycle14.txt unless a band break is traced and tuned in a small slice.
- Step 4: milestone review. Opus 5.5 reviews the whole cycle against the DESIGN_BIBLE compass, with the cycle log entries, diff stat, test counts, and balance output in the package.

## Cycle 15, Step 1 of 4: campaign scoring in the sim (2026-10-17)

Claimed this run: Step 1 only. Steps 2, 3, and 4 remain.

### What was built
- Builder: free OpenCode model opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free, through the fixed CLI (opencode v2.0.31). Four earlier models in the prescribed rotation returned Rate limit exceeded and made no changes: opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free, opencode/glm-5.3-flash-free, opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free, and opencode/longcat-2.5-preview-free. Nemotron accepted the call and completed in about 333 seconds.
- js/sim.js only, 63 insertions, no other file touched by the builder. CFG gains five scoring tunables: scorePerProvince 10, scorePerFactoryLevel 5, scorePerStrength 1, scoreOwnCapital 50, scoreEnemyCapital 100.
- campaignScore(state, nationId) is the one shared readout. It returns provinces and provincePoints, factoryLevels and factoryPoints, armyStrength (the rounded sum of surviving unit strength) and armyPoints, exchangeNet and exchangePoints (the raw net from the existing exchange ledger), ownCapitalHeld and ownCapitalPoints, enemyCapitalHeld and enemyCapitalPoints, and total, which is the sum of the five point fields. It reuses the existing helpers nationProvinces, factoryLevels, unitsOf, exchangeNet, and opposingNation.
- campaignResult(state) returns gameOver, winner, endReason, day, the player and enemy campaignScore objects, and margin (player total minus enemy total).
- Both functions are exported in the api object near the exchange exports. A header note and a section comment state that scoring is computed from current state only and that no rule reads it.

### Verification run by the orchestrator (not taken from the builder)
- Full git diff reviewed: only js/sim.js, only the changes listed above, no scope creep, no UI, test, or docs change by the builder.
- node --check on every JS file in js, tests, and tools: all pass.
- node --test tests/sim.test.js: 106 pass, 0 fail (suite unchanged this step; formal scoring tests are Step 3).
- node tools/balance.js all: byte identical to tools/baseline-cycle14.txt, so every band of Jash's 2026-10-11 ruling still holds exactly as recorded.
- Python byte scan for em and en dashes across the whole repo: zero.
- No rule reads the score, verified by grep: the only callers of campaignScore are campaignResult itself and the api export; tick does not call either function.
- Spot checks by the orchestrator: seed 1 at day 1, player total 542 (35 provinces for 350, 14 factory levels for 70, army strength 72 for 72, exchange 0, own capital 50, enemy capital 0) and enemy total 527 (35 provinces, 11 factory levels, same army and capital shape). Seed 42 at day 1, player 512 and enemy 522. A second call returns an identical object and does not mutate state. A full passive campaign on seed 1 ends on day 36 with winner enemy, player total minus 15, enemy total 1161, and margin minus 1176; the enemy score correctly records that it holds the player capital and the player score records that it does not hold its own.
- Honest observation, recorded and not fixed in this step: because exchangePoints is the raw exchange net, a heavily losing nation can finish with a negative total (the passive seed 1 player at minus 15 above). That is the arithmetic the brief specified, not a defect in the builder's work. Whether a total should floor at zero is a feel and legibility question: it is parked for Jash in DECISIONS_FOR_JASH.md item 14 and named for Step 3 and the Step 4 judge to consider, with no change made here.

### Lessons applied and learned
- Lessons applied: one step per run; legibility is law (every score component is a named, visible quantity the player already sees in play, with its weight in CFG); stackPower stays the one shared power function (scoring does not touch it); rebalance only in small slices (no tuning changed, balance byte identical by construction and by rerun).
- New lesson recorded in LOOP_LESSONS.md: the free model rotation worked as designed on its first live cycle step, with four rate limited models costing only seconds each and the fifth completing the build; and a score that includes a raw signed ledger can go negative, which must be surfaced as a design question instead of silently floored.

## 2. Grade Against the Compass

**HOI4 war heart: unchanged.**
- No production, division, frontline, or combat rule moved.
- The byte identical balance output proves it.
- This is correct for a readout cycle, and I record it as zero movement, not a gain.

**Civ VII visible progression: small gain, off the map.**
- The end screen makes the compounding loop countable: provinces, factory levels, and surviving army strength are the loop's own nouns.
- Nothing changed on the map itself, and the bible's progression test is a map test.
- The screen shows a final snapshot only. It never shows where the nation started.
- The core fantasy is "start weak, become visibly powerful," and a start versus end comparison would serve it directly.
- The prescription did not require that comparison, so it is a parked owner item, not a flag.

**EU5 lore: unchanged.**
- The end screen has no epilogue, no reference to national history, and no grudge resolution.
- Whether it should is a taste question. It is parked below.

**Legibility: real gain. This is the cycle's main contribution.**
- The run used to end on a one line banner. It now ends on a surface that says who won, why, on what day, how each number was earned, and that the score changes nothing.
- The loop enforced the bible's strictest clause twice, rejecting code vocabulary as an explanation and rejecting an incomplete exchange definition.
- The remaining copy issue, the clipped capital phrasing, is correctly recorded as taste.

## 3. Ruling on the Scoring Design as a Readout

**Component set: right for the bible.**
- Provinces, factory levels, and army strength are the three nouns of the compounding loop.
- Capitals are the existing decisive objectives.
- The exchange net is the scoreboard for the drone cost exchange, a signature mechanic: the bible literally says "the scoreboard tracks who bleeds money faster."
- The set leaves out the EW arms race, rail supply, and intel. That is acceptable. Those mechanics act through the other components, and scoring them separately would double count.

**Exchange at raw signed weight: it belongs, and signed is correct.**
- A cost exchange is a net by definition. Flooring it per component would hide exactly the bleeding the bible wants tracked.
- Shipping it raw rather than inventing a weight was the right call for the loop, since a weight is a balance and taste decision.

I note two concerns for the owner and decide neither:

1. **Unit scale.** The exchange net is in cost units while every other component is in authored points. In the passive seed 1 campaign its magnitude is evidently modest, since the player ends at minus 15. The package gives no distribution for drone heavy sensible play, where it could dominate the total or be noise. A readout only tool that prints per component scores across the 8 standard seeds and 3 paths would answer this without touching balance.
2. **Missing weight.** Exchange is the only component without a CFG weight. Adding scorePerExchange at 1 would change no number and make the weight set uniform. That is hygiene the owner may want, not a defect.

**Capital weighting: legible as described.**
- Own capital is worth 50 held. Enemy capital is worth 100 held.
- Each row states held or not held and the points.
- The asymmetry reads naturally: defending is expected, taking is exceptional.
- Losing your capital produces a 150 point swing between the two totals. That is visible as two separate rows, which is the legible way to show it.

**Does the screen explain itself at the moment the player reaches it: yes.** It shows:
- The result and the end reason.
- The day.
- Labelled rows with their earning rule.
- A margin line naming the leader with both totals.
- A statement that the win conditions, not the score, decided the outcome.

That meets "every system explains itself on screen at the moment the player touches it." One residual risk, parked below: a player who wins on conditions but trails on score. The margin line handles this factually, but the owner may want explicit wording for that case.

## 4. Cycle 16 Prescription: Save and Load

Ordering is owner directed: Cycle 16 save and load, then Cycle 17 playability. Loop rules apply: verify every step, revert on failure, and re-brief at half size on a second failure.

**Determinism facts the cycle must respect:**
- The sim draws seeded rng inside movement engagements.
- State holds records that a save must restore exactly: beats, textures, intel snapshots, and the exchange ledger.
- Therefore the save must capture the rng's internal position, not just the seed.
- The proof standard must be behavioral (continuation equivalence), not merely structural (roundtrip equality).

### Step 0, audit (no code; documentation only)

Produce STATE_INVENTORY.md listing every field reachable from state:
- Its type.
- Whether it is authoritative or derived (cache, index, adjacency).
- Whether it is aliased: the same object reachable by two paths, for example a unit referenced from a province and from a unit list.
- Every non-JSON value: Map, Set, undefined, NaN, Infinity, negative zero, functions, and class instances.

Locate the rng:
- State whether its internal state lives in state or in a module closure.
- Grep js/sim.js for Math.random, Date.now, performance.now, and any wall clock or frame time read.
- Confirm the Cycle 15 exchange wording question from Section 1.

**Exit criteria:**
- The inventory is complete and committed.
- The grep result is recorded.
- Every hazard has a named handling plan.
- No code changed.

### Step 1, sim: rng state into state (js/sim.js only)

**Goal.** Every input the sim needs to reproduce its own future lives in `state` as plain, JSON-safe data. Nothing determinism-relevant may live in module scope, closures, or the UI.

**Work.**
- Audit `js/sim.js` for every rng call site. Per-engagement rng is already derived from game seed, tick count, and a canonical engagement key. That means the derivation inputs, not a stream position, are what must be persisted: `state.seed` and `state.tick` as integers.
- If any call site draws from a module-level or long-lived stream (beat selection, texture selection, anything outside engagements), do one of two things. Either convert it to the same derived pattern with its own key namespace, or store the stream's internal state in `state.rng` as plain integers.
- Make the canonical engagement key independent of iteration order. Build it from sorted participant ids and the engagement location, never from object key order, Map or Set iteration, or array position that can change after a roundtrip. JSON roundtrips reorder integer-like object keys, so any key built by walking an object is suspect.
- Remove any `Math.random`, `Date.now`, or `performance.now` reachable from sim code.

**Exit criteria.**
1. A grep of `js/sim.js` and everything it imports shows zero `Math.random`, `Date.now`, and `performance.now` in sim paths.
2. No module-level mutable variable in sim code influences any outcome. Each remaining one is listed in the step notes with a reason it is inert.
3. A unit test shows the canonical engagement key is identical when participants are supplied in shuffled orders, and identical before and after a JSON roundtrip of the containing state.
4. Golden replays from Cycle 15 are unchanged. For at least five fixed seeds run to the end, the final state hash and the full event log are byte-identical to the pre-refactor outputs. Any difference fails the step. This is a refactor, not a balance change.

### Step 2, sim: serialize and deserialize (js/sim.js plus a new js/save.js)

**Work.**
- Add `serialize(state)` returning a JSON string with `saveVersion`, `seed`, `tick`, the full sim state, and a checksum over the canonical payload.
- Add `deserialize(string)` returning a fresh state or a typed error. It must never partially mutate an existing state.
- Restore exactly, without recomputation, the records the owner flagged:
  - **Campaign beats:** fired flags, pending beats and their scheduled ticks, and any per-beat counters. A loaded game must never re-fire a beat or skip one that was due.
  - **Recurring textures:** last-shown ticks, cooldowns, rotation position. These have zero mechanical effect, but they are still restored exactly so that the text a player sees continues identically.
  - **Intel snapshots:** stored as the stale values captured at snapshot time. Deserialize must not rebuild them from current truth, because that would leak information the player does not have.
  - **Exchange ledger:** restored as an ordered, append-only list with entry ids. Load must not replay entries into running totals a second time. Totals are either stored and checked against the ledger sum, or derived only from the ledger.
- Reject values JSON cannot carry faithfully at serialize time, with a named error: `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-0`, `undefined` in arrays, functions, Map, and Set. Silent coercion is not allowed.
- Reject on load: missing required fields, unknown `saveVersion`, and checksum mismatch. No silent defaulting of missing fields.

**Exit criteria.**
1. `serialize(deserialize(serialize(s)))` is byte-identical to `serialize(s)` for every state sampled in Step 4.
2. Deserialize of a corrupted, truncated, wrong-version, or field-missing save returns a typed error. The previously loaded state is untouched, verified by hash.
3. Serialize throws a named error on each forbidden value type, one test per type.
4. The ledger total after load equals the ledger total before save, and equals the sum of ledger entries.

### Step 3, UI: save and load controls (js/ui.js, index.html)

**Work.**
- Add Save and Load controls and at least one localStorage slot, plus export to and import from a file so saves survive a cleared browser.
- On load, discard every UI cache derived from state: selection, open panels, hover targets, intel panel contents, and any end screen render. Then rebuild from the loaded state.
- Show deserialize errors in plain language. A failed load leaves the current game running.
- Saving is allowed while paused or at any speed. The sim tick boundary is the only save point. The UI must never serialize mid-tick.

**Exit criteria.**
1. UI code holds no sim truth. A review of `js/ui.js` finds no field that, if lost, would change the sim's future.
2. A manual check covers saving mid-engagement, during a pending beat, and after an intel snapshot. After reload, the visible panels match what was shown before the save.
3. Importing a corrupted file shows the error message, and the running game continues unchanged.
4. Exporting and then importing a save produces a state hash equal to the original.

### Step 4, tests and balance: save integrity and time step determinism

**Proof standard.** Proof means behavioral continuation equivalence, not structural roundtrip equality. A roundtrip test proves the bytes survive. It does not prove the game continues the same way, because hidden inputs such as order-dependent keys, module state, and recomputed snapshots pass a roundtrip and still diverge later. Every determinism claim in this cycle is proven by running the future and comparing it.

**Save integrity tests (owner required).**
- Byte idempotence of serialize, deserialize, serialize, as in Step 2.
- Corruption, truncation, version, missing field, and checksum rejection, with no mutation of the live state.
- Forbidden value rejection, one test per type.
- Record-specific checks:
  - **Beats:** save on the exact tick a beat fires, and on the tick before it. The beat fires exactly once across the boundary.
  - **Textures:** the texture sequence after load matches the uninterrupted run.
  - **Intel:** a snapshot taken before save still shows its stale values after load, even when current truth has changed.
  - **Ledger:** entry count, order, ids, and totals match. No duplicate entries appear after repeated save and load cycles.

**Time step determinism tests (owner required).**
- The sim outcome depends only on the sequence of ticks, never on how wall clock time was batched into them. For each test seed, compare final state hash and full event log across three runs: advancing one tick per call, advancing in large batches, and an irregular mix with speed changes and pauses. All three must be identical.
- The same comparison is repeated with a save and load inserted at an arbitrary point in each schedule.

**Behavioral continuation equivalence tests.**
- **Run A:** seed S, run to tick T, serialize, deserialize into a fresh state with no shared objects (and in a fresh module instance where the harness allows), then run to tick T+K.
- **Run B:** seed S, run uninterrupted to T+K.
- **Required:** the final state hash is identical, the full event log from T to T+K is identical, and the exchange ledger, beat records, texture records, and intel snapshots are deep-equal at T+K.
- **Sampling of T:**
  - tick 0
  - mid-engagement, while an engagement's rng is in use
  - the tick a campaign beat fires
  - immediately after an intel snapshot
  - immediately after a ledger entry
  - one tick before the end condition
- **Chained case:** save and load at several ticks in one run, compared against the uninterrupted run.
- **Seeds:** at least five, covering a passive seed, an engagement-heavy seed, and a campaign-beat-heavy seed.

**What must be proven about engagement rng specifically.** Given identical seed, tick, and canonical key, an engagement produces identical draws whether or not a save and load occurred before it. The canonical key must also be identical before and after load for every engagement in the sampled runs. The harness logs each engagement key and draw count in both runs and diffs them, so that a divergence points at the engagement that caused it rather than only at the final hash.

**Widened zero mechanical effect coverage (carried from Section 1).** The Cycle 15 test proved zero mechanical effect for recurring textures on one passive seed only. Extend it to the full Step 4 seed set, including the engagement-heavy and beat-heavy seeds. Also run it across a save and load boundary. For each seed, run with textures active and with texture selection stubbed out. The mechanical state hash, meaning all state excluding texture records and text, must be identical at every sampled tick.

**Balance.** No balance changes this cycle. The balance check is that the Cycle 15 golden outcomes for the fixed seeds are unchanged after Steps 1 through 3.

**Exit criteria.**
1. All save integrity tests pass.
2. All time step determinism tests pass on every test seed.
3. All continuation equivalence tests pass for every sampled T on every seed, including the chained case.
4. The engagement key and draw-count diff is empty in every comparison.
5. Widened zero mechanical effect coverage passes on all seeds, including across save and load.
6. Golden outcomes are unchanged.
7. Any test failure is fixed at the cause in sim code. The tolerance is not loosened, and a sampled tick is not dropped to make a failure go away.

### Step 5, milestone review

**The judge confirms:**
- Step 1 through Step 4 exit criteria were met, with evidence: test output, grep results, and golden hash comparison.
- No determinism-relevant data lives outside `state`.
- Beats, textures, intel snapshots, and the ledger are restored exactly and not recomputed.
- The proof offered is continuation equivalence, not only roundtrip equality.
- The Step 0 end screen wording check below was done and recorded.

**Exit criteria.** All of the above are confirmed, or any gap is assigned to Cycle 17 with a named owner step.

### Carry-over addendum to Step 0 (from Section 1)

Before Step 1 begins, open the rendered end screen in a browser, at least once on a finished game. Read the exchange conversion wording as displayed and confirm it matches the intended meaning of the ledger conversion. Record the exact rendered text in the step notes. This is a read-and-confirm item only. Any wording change it suggests goes to Section 5 if it is a taste call, or to a later cycle if it is a correctness fix. It does not expand Cycle 16 scope.

## Section 5: Taste level items parked for the human owner

These are in addition to DECISIONS item 14 (score floor at zero, and whether the weights feel right), which remains parked. None is decided here.

1. **Start versus end comparison on the end screen.** Whether the end screen should show where the empire began next to where it finished, as a side-by-side summary. This is a presentation and pacing choice for the owner.

2. **Lore epilogue on the end screen.** Whether a short narrative epilogue should accompany the final numbers, and how much text the end screen should carry. This is a tone call.

3. **Wording for winning on conditions while trailing on score.** Whether the end screen should say explicitly when a player met the victory conditions but finished behind on score, and in what voice. The mechanics are settled. How the game names this outcome is the owner's call.

4. **Exchange unit scale.** Whether exchange values should be shown at their current scale or rescaled so the numbers read more naturally to a player. This affects how the ledger and conversion feel, not what they compute.

5. **Missing uniform exchange weight.** Whether exchange categories should share one uniform weight in scoring, or keep the current arrangement with no uniform weight defined. This touches how score feels, so it sits alongside item 14 for the owner rather than being settled by the judge.

## Cycle 16, Step 2 of 5: serialize and deserialize, sim layer (2026-10-18)

Claimed this run: Step 2 only (serialize and deserialize). Step 3 (UI save and load controls) does not start this run.

### What was built
- One new file, `js/save.js` (331 lines), in the same dual browser and node pattern as js/sim.js and js/lore.js (window.AshesSave and module.exports). js/sim.js is unchanged: no sim change was needed, because Step 1 already exported the hash surface and the save format needs nothing from the sim. The recorded step list names js/sim.js in this step's scope; the honest record is that the work landed entirely in the new file.
- Exports, exactly as briefed: SAVE_VERSION (1), serializeSave, deserializeSave, checksumFor.
- serializeSave(state) returns { ok: true, text } where text is a JSON envelope string with fields in this order: saveVersion, seed, tick (state.tickCount), checksum, payload. The payload is a JSON string of the state with the edges key omitted and every other top level key in its original order, so edgeList is the one saved edge representation (STATE_INVENTORY.md section 7). checksumFor is FNV-1a over the payload string with the sim's own constants (2166136261, 16777619, Math.imul), returned as a decimal string. serializeSave does not mutate its input and never throws for the rejected cases below.
- Serialize time rejection: before stringifying, a recursive walk of the saved state refuses any value JSON cannot carry faithfully (a function, undefined, a symbol, a bigint, NaN, Infinity, negative Infinity, or a circular reference) with { ok: false, kind: "unserializable", field, reason }, the field naming the exact path (for example units[0].attritionCarry) and the reason in plain words. The cycle guard tracks ancestors on the current path only, so a shared object on two branches is allowed and only a true loop is refused; a state missing its edge list, or whose edge list is not a list, returns kind "missing".
- deserializeSave(text) never throws and returns { ok: true, state } or { ok: false, kind, reason } with kinds in the briefed set: "not-a-save" (not a non empty string, envelope not JSON, envelope not a plain object, payload not a string), "missing" (an envelope header field absent, or a parsed payload missing any of the 18 required saved state keys, the field named), "version" (saveVersion present but not 1), "checksum" (checksumFor over the payload string differs from the header), "corrupt" (payload not JSON, payload seed or tickCount disagreeing with the header, edgeList not a list, or an edge entry without string endpoints). Checks run in that order, so a wrong version reports as version and a tampered payload reports as checksum.
- Restoration: beats, textures, exchange, and intel are restored exactly as parsed; no sim function is called and nothing is recomputed. The edges lookup is rebuilt from edgeList with the sim's edgeKey rule (the two endpoint ids sorted as strings, joined with a vertical bar), each edges entry the identical object as its edgeList entry. The returned top level object is built in the createGame key order with edges in its createGame position, so a restored state's JSON text matches the original state's JSON text byte for byte. Nulls stay null and fractional numbers are never rounded or coerced.

### Compass criticism (judge)
- Legibility: the save card meets the floor with plain language errors, but it does not yet tell the player what a save contains, when the slot was last written and at what day and nation, that loading replaces the current game, or what just happened after a load. A first time player who clicks Load and sees the map jump with selection cleared has no on screen confirmation; the judge called that a small Stellaris failure and assigned it to Cycle 17.
- Visible progression (Civ VII): nothing changed on the map this cycle, and the judge graded that defensible for exactly one cycle: the 2026-10-11 ruling ordered this work, determinism and save integrity are preconditions for every later balance slice being trustworthy, and save and load lets a player keep a campaign long enough to watch the country grow. It is not defensible as a pattern; Cycle 17 is player facing, which is the correct correction.
- Signature systems: restoring the exchange ledger and intel snapshots exactly, without recomputation, protects the drone cost exchange and intel as sight signatures across a save boundary; the right thing to have guarded.
- Balance ruling: intact. Balance byte identical to baseline-cycle14 on all standard seeds, no rebalance happened.

### Gaps (judge; not flags, no evidence of a defect; owners assigned)
- G1: determinism relevant data outside state is not stated as a confirmed negative. Section 9 lists 15 UI held rows and Step 3 discards them on load, but the package never states that none of the 15 feeds the sim, and continuation equivalence runs in a harness that may bypass main.js; the Step 1 summary also omits the wall clock grep sim path result as an explicit record. Owner: Cycle 17 Step 0 (classification, grep record, and the confirmed negative sentence; the harness bypass hole either closed by citation or owned by Step 4 as one browser driven continuation check).

Close G1: classify each of the 15 Section 9 UI held rows as sim relevant or not with read and write citations (state is sim relevant by definition, with a check that main.js never writes a sim field directly; selections must hand orders to a sim function in the same handler with nothing queued in main.js; paused, speed, and the timer are cadence only if the batching determinism test covers every speed value; pauseBeforeOverlay only restores the paused flag; card and notice state is render only unless a dismissal calls into the sim; urlSeed is consumed exactly once in newGame and load ignores it; el holds DOM references only), Section 9 of STATE_INVENTORY.md gains the classification column, and the step entry states the confirmed negative in one sentence or names the exceptions. Write the saveVersion rule (any payload shape change bumps the version; an unknown or older version migrates through a named tested function or rejects in plain language, never loads silently; meta state never enters the sim payload; Step 4 owns the rejection message wording). Tag every gap with its owning step (1 to 4) or PARKED with a one line reason. Prescription: Cycle 17 step 5 judge, Cycle 18 Step 4, planned in CYCLE_18_STEP0_SPEC.md section 5. Claimed this run: Step 4 only. Step 5 (cycle close and milestone review) is next and does not start this run.

### Scope, stated before the brief was written
- tools/navy-check.js already proves part of this step's ground: its Run 1 asserts the navy explain rule text on an unmodified game, and its Run 3 stages a blockade by flotilla control and asserts both blockade loss numbers and both coastal counts on the card against a node mirror. The card showed a loss number and a general rule paragraph; nothing said the Dominion is blockaded today, how many of its home coastal provinces the player controls against the threshold, or the same facts for the player.
